Sports.title: Fifa accused of ‘selling the soul of football’ over $20bn World Cup commercial rights sale plan
Sports.content:
Fifa has announced plans to sell the commercial rights to its tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors in a controversial move that triggered an immediate backlash from Uefa, leading European clubs and politicians.

Uefa released a strongly worded statement accusing Fifa of “attempting to sell the soul of football” and is believed to be considering its legal position, while sources at numerous elite clubs were highly critical of the proposal in private. Andy Burnham, the UK’s new prime minister, condemned the move.

Fifa has confirmed it is working with the US bank JP Morgan on setting up a new entity – to be called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) – that would raise hundreds of millions of dollars by selling a significant stake in the commercial rights of the men’s and women’s World Cups, and the Club World Cup to investors, with promises of an increase in distribution of “over $10bn” (£7.5bn) then being redistributed back to Fifa’s 211 member associations.

Thrive Capital, an investment company founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of Donald Trump’s son‑in-law Jared Kushner – is leading the search for investors.

Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said the plan would see “the commercial side of the game [operating] as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world”. The plans are subject to approval by a “majority” of member associations, but Fifa declined to comment when asked when a vote will take place.

Numerous sources with knowledge of Fifa’s proposals said it is valuing the new commercial venture at about $20bn, with Infantino looking to cash in on football’s growing global popularity after this summer’s World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico. The Guardian revealed this month that Fifa’s revenues for the tournament would exceed $15bn, a significant increase on the projected figure of $13bn, with such growth appearing to embolden Infantino to seek further riches.

The revelation of the plans provoked an immediate backlash from Uefa, with the European governing body accusing Fifa of attempting to sell the soul of football. Relations between the two most powerful organisations in the sport are at an all-time low, with Uefa claiming Fifa undermined the integrity of the World Cup this month when it intervened to overturn the USA striker Falorin Balogun’s red card after Trump called onasked Infantino to do so.

“This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” Uefa said of the FFE plan. “Uefa takes it extremely seriously. So should every national football association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game. The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino is looking to cash in on football’s growing global popularity following this summer’s World Cup. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

Burnham, an Everton fan, posted on social media: “Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine. The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.”

Infantino had succeeded in keeping Fifa’s plans under wraps until reports of the proposal first emerged in the Times and Financial Times. Fifa council members are understood to have been surprised by the announcement, having been sidelined from the decision‑making process.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is the second occasion that Infantino has attempted to attract private capital to fund Fifa. In 2018, he agreed a deal in principle with the Japanese bank SoftBank to provide $25bn in funding for an expanded Club World Cup and global Nations League, but failed to get sufficient support, largely due to opposition from Europe. Uefa and the clubs are again united against Fifa’s plans, but Infantino may have enough backing from elsewhere to be able to disregard them.

In its statement, Fifa said the new enterprise would enable it to increase the funding provided to each of the associations from $8m to $20m each year, a huge sum for the majority of their 211 members.

Fifa also insisted it would retain responsibility for football’s governance and the international match calendar, but in reality inviting private investment in its commercial rights would subject the decision makers to significant external pressures. External investors could ultimately be given significant influence over decisions that affect the entire sport, leading to fears they would seek to stage the World Cup more regularly and permit it to be hosted in only the most lucrative markets, such as the US. Fifa said it would “carefully select long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests in FFE – all net benefits of FFE will be reinvested back into football worldwide”.

Infantino is expected to be re‑elected unopposed as president next year despite the huge controversy he attracts, but under Fifa statutes must stand down in 2031 after serving three full terms. The Times reported, however, that Infantino has aspirations to serve as chair of the new commercial company, which could earn him tens of millions of dollars.

Sports.title: Retaining Rodri is key to Manchester City success under Enzo Maresca
Sports.content:
“Welcome home,” was Khaldoon al-Mubarak’s warm greeting to Enzo Maresca on his appointment last month as Manchester City manager. Now, after two previous spells at the club, the Italian’s task is to keep the chair content, and ensure a three-year contract does not end early. To achieve that, Maresca’s tenure must continue Pep Guardiola’s glittering legacy of 20 trophies across a decade of excellence.

The key to the 46-year-old, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2022-23 treble season and City’s elite development squad leader two years before that, being successful can be summed up in two words: “Keep Rodri”. Yet with Real Madrid almost certain to launch a bid for the peerless No 6, and him seemingly wanting to play for the Spanish giants, a move away from City may become inevitable.

Maresca’s best hope of avoiding “doing a David Moyes” – who succeeded Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in May 2013 and lasted a mere 34 Premier League games – and thriving as the man who follows the man is to retain Rodri, who has just captained Spain to World Cup glory, winning the Golden Ball as best player in the process. The 30-year-old is contracted until June. City’s stance is that they have no wish to sell and remain intent on persuading him to sign the new terms that have been on offer for a while.

Saying City will definitely be contenders for the biggest prizes next season if they retain Rodri may sound simplistic until you examine his CV and are reminded of the pivotal role he has played for the club. Rodri was key to City’s treble glory, including scoring the winner in the Champions League final against Inter. Then there was the 74-game unbeaten sequence with him in the colours that ran from February 2023 to May 2024. “He’s unbelievable, irreplaceable,” said Guardiola. “The best midfielder in the world by far.”

The World Cup triumph also came after Rodri had been part of Spain’s Euro 2024 glory and City’s 2023 Club World Cup success, again winning the player of the tournament in each. In the two seasons before the World Cup, injury plagued him, however. The result: no Premier League titles in either year for City, halting a record four-in-a-row run for Guardiola’s garlanded team.

Rodri’s ability to mould and control contests was reiterated by his World Cup displays. Exhibit A: the chokehold imposed on France in the semi-finals. At domestic and international level, this is a priceless quality. So if Maresca can field Rodri, City will be feared in the league and on the continent. The back injury for which Rodri underwent surgery on Monday is minor, but the desire to broaden his club horizons – primarily in Spain – remains, meaning there is no certainty he will stay put. Particularly so given the initial resistance of Real Madrid’s president, Florentino Pérez, to acquiring Rodri has shifted, due, surely, to his resurgence at the World Cup and maybe José Mourinho, returning as head coach, expressing a need for the player’s calm and elan.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca worked under Pep Guardiola as Manchester City won the treble in 2023. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

City have invested £116m on Elliot Anderson this summer, an England first-choice midfielder who may be joined by another midfielder in Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, the 18-year-old who also impressed at the World Cup for Morocco, and would cost around £85m. However, neither of them or Tijjani Reijnders, Mateo Kovacic nor Nico González can claim to be in the class of Rodri, who may well be in line to claim a second Ballon d’Or following his World Cup exploits.

Maresca won the Championship with Leicester in 2024 and the following season led Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and to a Conference League triumph, following that up with glory at the expanded Club World Cup, which featured the 3-0 demolition of Paris Saint-Germain in the final. All of this convinced al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano, that Maresca is the one who can thrive after the era-defining Guardiola.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Gvardiol says 'great things' will happen under Maresca Show Joško Gvardiol has signed a new five-year contract with Manchester City, the defender stating that “great things” can be achieved with Enzo Maresca, the new manager. While the terms include an option of a further 12-months, the Croatian is confident that the Italian’s first season will be successful. “I remember when he was at Chelsea [2024-26] it was difficult to play against them – especially away. We struggled. He’s here and I think we can achieve some great things together,” Gvardiol said. The 24-year-old has made 122 appearances and claimed six trophies with City since joining from RB Leipzig in 2023 for £77m and was voted the club’s 2024-5 player of the season. Gvardiol said: “I remember my first season when I arrived – back then I was kind of still young. In these three years I’ve learned a lot of things from all my team-mates, my friends in the dressing room and on the pitch in the last three years. "I still think there are a lot of things to improve and learn but I’m only 24, I have enough time.” Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

However, as Maresca made clear with his “after Sir Alex [Ferguson]” reference in his unveiling on Friday, directly following greatness can be treacherous. The comparison between him and Moyes is hardly precise, though. Moyes arrived at United trophyless and with no experience of the pressures of an elite club. Maresca’s résumé shows a season and a half in the Chelsea hothouse and, with his prior experience of City, he is versed in the organisation where he now plays a crucial role.

City have five weeks of the market remaining to try to persuade Rodri his future is at the club. Guardiola’s stance was never to stop any player exiting who wished to do so. The logic is understandable: what is the point in retaining an unhappy employee? In this case it would also be one who wants to return to his native city. “Having played for Atlético [Madrid] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid,” Rodri said in March. “There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

Even Real Madrid boycotting Rodri’s Ballon d’Or-crowning ceremony in November 2024 in protest at Vinícius Júnior’s failure to win the vote has clearly not dissuaded the midfielder that the Bernabéu can be the home al-Mubarak characterises City as for Maresca.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso plays down Welbeck and Henderson moves after Chelsea win
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing the veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson after his first game in charge of the team, a 6-4 pre-season victory against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, but said he was looking to build a squad that had “proper balance”.

Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a surprise move to sign the 35-year-old Welbeck from Brighton, with the club also reportedly interested in signing the 36-year-old Henderson from Brentford. The links to two Premier League stalwarts reflects a revised transfer strategy under Alonso, with Chelsea seeking to recruit more experienced players into their squad as opposed to focused solely on signing young players, often tying them to lengthy contracts.

“I’m sure that from today to the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of links, a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them, it’s going to be a hard task,” Alonso said. “But for sure, we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance. We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team.”

The new Chelsea manager fielded a youthful side at the Accor Stadium at Sydney Olympic Park in Homebush, with Liam Delap and Tosin Adarabioyo the most experienced members of the starting lineup. Alonso waited until the 63rd minute to bring on a host of star names, including Cole Palmer and João Pedro. The Brazilian forward, who missed out on a place in Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad, made a significant impact off the bench, scoring a hat-trick in just nine minutes as Chelsea took control of the game against their A-League opponents.

João Pedro scored 20 goals during an excellent debut season for Chelsea, having arrived from Brighton for £60m 12 months ago, and asked about the player’s mood before the upcoming campaign, Alonso said: “Very hungry. João is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to, after a great last year, when he scored many goals. He wants to keep scoring more and more.”

A number of Chelsea’s youngsters showed plenty of promise, with the 17-year-old Dastan Satpayev opening the scoring after six minutes. The Kazakh forward is yet to sign officially for the club and is playing in pre-season as a triallist. His opening goal came from a defence-splitting pass from another teenager, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, with Satpayev smashing the ball home at the near post.

Chelsea’s back four struggled in the first half against a lively Wanderers frontline and their reported new set-piece coach, Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee, will have plenty to work on judging by the ease with which Brandon Borrello and Anthony Pantazopoulos won headers from a corner as the latter scored at the back post for the hosts.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming on as a second-half substitute. Photograph: Mark Evans/EPA

The Wanderers took the lead through Aydan Hammond before a lovely finish from the Portuguese midfielder Dário Essugo made it 2-2 at the break. The goals kept coming in the second half when the left-back Landon Emenalo, who impressed going forward, saw his clearance deflected into the path of Dylan Scicluna, who put the Sydney side 3-2 ahead. Alonso then turned to his bench and his substitutions made an immediate impact. João Pedro held off a number of challenges on the edge of the box before pulling the ball back to Jamie Gittens, who fired home from close range.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But this topsy-turvy game, which felt like England’s third-place playoff against France at the World Cup and finished with the same scoreline, provided more entertainment as the Australian side went ahead for a third time after Estêvão Willian lost possession on the edge of his own area. Awan Lual was on hand to slide the ball through Robert Sánchez’s legs to put his side 4-3 ahead.

The Wanderers, who are also in pre-season, again failed to hold on to a lead as Chelsea overpowered a team that finished bottom of their domestic league last season. João Pedro looked sharp as he showed great composure to score twice in five minutes, before scrambling home an effort from a corner to wrap up his match-winning exploits.

João Pedro’s performance was in stark contrast to that of Delap, who has been repeatedly linked with a move away from west London. The 23-year-old endured another frustrating evening for Chelsea, going close on two occasions but failing to find the back of the net. Assessing Delap’s attitude since returning from the summer break, Alonso said: “I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good and he’s doing great.”

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò, said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: Wrexham face Liverpool with Premier League still in their sights despite setback
Sports.content:
The Wrexham co-owner Ryan Reynolds called it a “punch-me moment” – his club playing Liverpool in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium just five years after he and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) completed their takeover of a club languishing in the National League. The knockout blow would be playing Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League in 2027-28 and the manager, Phil Parkinson, accepts there is expectation on Wrexham to complete their remarkable rise through the divisions next season.

Parkinson’s team face Liverpool with confidence in the Bronx on Wednesday having defeated Manchester United and Leeds in pre-season so far and moved on from the anguish of missing out on the Championship playoffs on the final day of last season. The near-miss was undoubtedly a setback to an ambitious club’s grand vision but finishing seventh in the Championship at the first time of asking, Parkinson insists, was an accomplishment that should not be dismissed lightly.

The Wrexham manager said: “If we’re honest, to say five years down the line we’d have finished seventh in the Championship we would have said that was going to take some going. To get three promotions back-to-back-to-back is unheralded. Even though there’s always been ambition within the club and we’ve had resources, to take the club from the National League to seventh in the Championship is a lot of big steps and particularly the one last year. League One to the Championship is a huge step.

“Of course we would have loved to have got in the playoffs but I think the staff and the players should be really very proud of their achievements because that was a tough ask, especially with making so many changes.”

Wrexham are among the favourites for promotion next season but are the only Championship club not to make a signing – though a deal for Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray is close – and will not be the only well-funded team with that aim, given the parachute payments available to relegated West Ham, Burnley and Wolves.

“I think the division is going to be stronger this season with the teams coming down,” Parkinson says. “We’ve got work to do within the squad to make us competitive again. We’re close to one signing but we need several more before the window closes. We have to be patient and we will be, but the squad’s not where we want it to be, to be competitive to meet the demands of a Championship season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing the newspaper’s 2005 headline when Zinedine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French Football Federation headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground Métro tracks with flags, flares and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact that Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach entered the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, said after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinedine Zidane is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo said. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Bleus’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.”

Zidane declared it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy. I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager. I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.” The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would retain the armband, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” he said when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he said playfully.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi‑finals. “I spent 25 years in Spain and you know what that means,” he said, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first internationals of the new season. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it. It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane said, is on his first match in charge, which will be in Turkey on 25 September.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off
Sports.content:
Sunderland are poised to sign the long-time Newcastle target Dayann Methalie from Toulouse. The France Under-21s defender, who can play left-back or wingback and also operate in the centre, has attracted widespread interest this summer but Régis Le Bris now appears close to acquiring him for about £26m.

Newcastle had extensively scouted Methalie, who made 27 Ligue 1 appearances for Toulouse last season, and reportedly tried to sign him in January. The club have now indicated they opted against the idea of recruiting the 20-year-old and have not submitted a bid this summer. Nonetheless, Methalie appeared an ideal fit for Newcastle’s new transfer policy of recruiting young players in the £20m-£40m price bracket.

Sunderland can offer the 6ft 2in defender Europa League football and he is understood to have verbally agreed a five-year deal at the Stadium of Light, where he would not merely be coached by a compatriot in Le Bris but be part of a sizeable contingent of French-speaking players including Enzo Le Fée, Nordi Mukiele and Habib Diarra. Methalie will be Le Bris’s second summer signing after the arrival of the Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who arrived on a free transfer after leaving Lille.

While Methalie is likely to face considerable competition from Reinildo to establish himself as Sunderland’s first-choice left-back, his amalgam of impressive recovery pace, robust physicality and assured left foot have seen him shine as a left-sided central defender in a back three and a back four.

Newcastle, meanwhile, remain in the market for cover at left-back and right-back, with the latter position one Eddie Howe is particularly anxious to reinforce after Kieran Trippier’s departure at the end of last season.

Howe’s hopes of keeping Bruno Guimarães appear to still rest on Arsenal’s willingness or otherwise to pay a fee in the region of £80m for the 28-year-old captain, who has been on a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil and is due to return to Newcastle on Friday, before travelling to a training camp at La Manga with the rest of the first-team squad.

Joe Willock’s future at St James’ Park also remains uncertain. Although Newcastle have rejected an offer in the region of £10m from Besiktas for the former Arsenal midfielder, they appear open to selling him, albeit for a fee closer to £20m.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United to sign Juve’s Francisco Conceição?
Sports.content:
As sports fans everywhere eagerly await the resumption of cricket’s County Championship season, what better way to while away a few minutes than to contemplate the latest football transfer rumours?

Manchester United and Michael Carrick want to sign the 23-year-old Portugal winger Francisco Conceição from Juventus. The tricky former Porto player, who recently returned from the World Cup, is valued at about £43m (€50m). United are also said to be ahead of Chelsea in the race to snap up Alex Scott from Bournemouth.

Real Madrid, meanwhile, have increased their offer to RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande – whom Leipzig had hoped to replace with Conceição – to about £98m. Reports in Germany say further talks are in order to get the deal for the 19-year-old Côte d’Ivoire international over the line.

Liverpool have emerged as favourites to sign the France international Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, having reportedly held preliminary talks with the 23-year-old over a lucrative transfer.

Bruno Guimarães continues to be the subject of strong interest from the Premier League champions, Arsenal. Newcastle, naturally, have insisted the Brazilian is not for sale, but personal terms have reportedly been agreed between the Gunners and Guimarães’s people, so a bid is surely imminent. Arsenal are also being linked with Vinícius Júnior, with Mikel Arteta apparently determined to sign the Madrid and Brazil forward. Speculation reached fever pitch on Tuesday when it was reported Vinícius would not train this week, further increasing uncertainty over his future. José Mourinho is keen to keep the winger.

Paris Saint-Germain have distanced themselves from a move the for all-conquering Manchester City midfielder Rodri, but the Premier League club expect an offer from Real Madrid.

Seemingly having fought off Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka, Sunderland are ready to boost their defensive options by signing the full-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

Over in Spain, it has been reported that Sevilla are ready to sell Ruben Vargas for about £17m and Aston Villa, Newcastle and Brighton are among potential suitors in His Majesty’s Premier League.

Leeds are poised to confirm a £40m deal for James Trafford, who re-signed for Manchester City after a couple of seasons at Burnley, while Manchester United are keen to send Joshua Zirkzee on a season-long loan to Juventus, with an option for the Bianconeri to buy the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea have held talks with the Brighton forward Danny Welbeck (35) and are also keen to sign Jordan Henderson (36). Welbeck knocked in 13 Premier League goals for the Seagulls last season and was fancied as a possible option for England at the World Cup, while Henderson made the cut, only to suffer a freak wrist injury. Chelsea are presumably drawing up eight-year contracts for both veterans.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund have agreed to sign the midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas from Racing Genk in Belgium, for a fee that could rise to £32m.

And John Stones, a free agent after leaving Manchester City, has moved closer to completing his move to Inter as reported in these pages: a deal has been verbally agreed.

Sports.title: Coventry smash club-record transfer as they sign in-demand Premier League player
Sports.content:
Coventry City have completed the signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth in a club-record £22.5million deal, talkSPORT understands.

Rushworth spent last season on loan at Coventry from Brighton, helping the Sky Blues get promoted to the Premier League.



3 Rushworth played a big role in Coventry's promotion Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Brighton had rejected a £20million bid from the newly-promoted side in June.

But the clubs have now finalised an agreement that will see the English goalkeeper join permanently. The £22.5m deal includes a sell-on and buy-back option for the Seagulls.

The 24-year-old starred for the Sky Blues as they stormed to the Championship title last season.



Rushworth played every league game for Frank Lampard's side, conceding just 45 goals and keeping 17 clean sheets.

New transfer record

The deal sees Coventry blow their current transfer record out of the water.



talkSPORT understands

They broke their record earlier this summer, with the £15.4m arrival of Aurele Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt.

It also represents a coup for Coventry, with other Premier League sides monitoring Rushworth earlier this summer.



The goalkeeper only had one year left on his deal, and he has been watched by England on multiple occasions.

Coventry's record signings Aurele Amenda (Frankfurt) - £15.4m - 2026 Haji Wright (Antalyaspor) - £7.7m - 2023 Craig Bellamy (Norwich) - £6.5m - 2000 Robbie Keane (Wolves) - £6m - 1999 Jack Rudoni (Huddersfield) - £5m - 2024

Huge fan

After playing every minute in the Championship, Lampard made it clear that he is a huge Rushworth fan.

Speaking about the goalkeeper last campaign, he said that England caps were waiting for him.

3 Coventry made another move for Rushworth after having a bid turned down Credit: Getty



He said: "Yes, for sure [he could play for his country]. I mean, without telling any England manager what to do…

"I know Jordan Pickford, who I worked with (at Everton), and is an incredible goalkeeper, and the goalkeepers are around him.

"But Rushy, just to isolate him, he’s got absolutely the talent to be able to play for his country, in my opinion.

"He just needs to keep working, but the levels he’s playing at are really, really good, and he’s been a big signing for us."



Coventry's transfer plans

talkSPORT also reported in June that Coventry had been weighing up a move for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Southampton captain missed out on the chance at promotion to the top-flight due to the Saints sending an intern to spy on Middlesbrough ahead of the play-off semi-final first leg.

3 Lampard will lead Coventry into the Premier League for the first time in 25 years Credit: Getty

They have since signed defender Amenda from Frankfurt too.

But there is plenty more business expected to be made by Lampard, who, speaking on The Sports Bar with Jason Cundy and Jamie O'Hara after winning promotion, admitted there was lots to do.



The Chelsea legend said in May: "We've got a lot of work to do. We'll do it quickly, and I think I feel like we have to do it quickly.

"It's the owner's choice, a lot of these things, because he's the boss man in the football club. But the conversations obviously have to happen quickly, but also enjoy this little moment."

Sports.title: Footballer dragged out of car by armed gang in terrifying robbery as club gives statement
Sports.content:
Footballer dragged out of car by armed gang in terrifying robbery as club gives statement

Police have made an arrest after a Union Saint-Gilloise footballer was the victim of a violent robbery last weekend.

Footage posted on social media shows striker Mohammed Fuseini being attacked on the streets of Brussels on Sunday morning.

2 Fuseini was attacked by robbers in a terrifying ordeal on Sunday Credit: Getty

Fuseini was dragged out of his car by masked individuals and held in a headlock during the terrifying scenes.

Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws (HLN) say the 24-year-old had his Rolex, worth between €8,000 and €14,000, stolen in the incident.

The attackers then fled the scene, with one of Fuseini's teammates said to have captured the attack on film.

It is said to have taken place close to the exit of Bloody Louis, which is a nightclub in central Brussels.

Union SG released a statement on Fuseini's condition which, via HLN, said: "The images from last Sunday are particularly harrowing.

"He subsequently went to the hospital for a check-up and received excellent care there from the Brussels police, whom we sincerely thank for their outstanding work.

"The injuries are not serious, and he resumed training yesterday."

"Three people were the victims of a robbery with violence as they made their way to their vehicle in Brussels," the public prosecutors office said.

"According to the initial findings of the investigation, several people allegedly attacked them and took various valuable items, including watches, telephones, and personal belongings."

A 23-year-old suspect has been arrested, with the office adding: "During a search of his home, items reported stolen were recovered.

"The Brussels Public Prosecutor's Office requested an investigating judge and asked for the suspect's detention.

"The suspect was charged with theft with violence committed by a gang and placed under an arrest warrant."

Following their arrest, the suspect is being held in Haren prison and his lawyer did not confirm if the watches were located at his home.

"I do not want to say anything more about that, because the judicial investigation is still ongoing," Samuel Rosenblatt said.

"My client is aware of the seriousness of the facts and regrets them," he added.

Fuseini joined Union SG in 2024 from Austrian side SK Sturm Graz.

2 Fuseini is said to have had his watch stolen during the attack Credit: Getty

He has scored 14 goals in 71 appearances for the club, with whom he has won the Belgian Pro League and Belgian Cup.

The forward has made two Champions League appearances at Union SG against Bayern Munich and Atalanta.

Fuseini also faced Scottish giants Rangers during the 2024/25 Europa League league phase.

He has made two appearances for Ghana and scored one goal in a 4-0 friendly win over Trinidad and Tobago last year.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s hopes of signing Vinicius Jr fade as Real Madrid step up contract talks
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s hopes of signing Vinicius Jr fade as Real Madrid step up contract talks

Jose Mourinho wants Vinicius Junior to stay at Real Madrid, who are working on talks to extend his contract, talkSPORT understands.

Real are determined not to lose their superstar on a free and they hope he'll sign a new deal, with progress being made this week.



3 Real Madrid are hopeful that Vini Jr will sign a new contract rather than leave Credit: Getty

Arsenal only ever explored the idea of signing the Brazilian internally and always knew the Spanish giants wanted to keep him.

It means the Gunners' hopes of signing Vinicius Jr. appear to be slipping following their initial interest in the winger.

The Premier League champions had contemplated making a move, but he was only a transfer option and not a key target.



talkSPORT reported on Monday that they have the finances available to make Vini Jr. their highest-paid player and they were prepared to open talks if they were given any encouragement from him.

Reports claim the 26-year-old Brazilian has been seeking as much as €550,000 (£470,000) on his next contract.



That would see him overtake Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's highest earner by a massive margin, with the England international earning £300,000 a week.

However, with Mourinho wanting to keep Vini Jr. at Real Madrid, his move to North London is looking unlikely.



He was also offered to Liverpool, but they opted not to pursue him - and he could now sign a new deal at Real soon.

If Vini Jr stays in Spain, he will be part of a squad that includes multiple new faces signed by Mourinho this summer.

Yan Diomande is set to join from RB Leipzig, following Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Denzel Dumfries through the door at the Bernabeu.

3 Mourinho wants to keep his Brazilian superstar at the club this summer Credit: Getty



3 It means Arsenal are set to miss out on another big name they were interested in Credit: Getty

Missing out on another star

Arsenal have been hoping to bring in a star forward this summer, but they are now set to miss out on another target.

If Vinicius Jr. doesn't make the move and stays at Real Madrid, the Gunners will have failed to sign him or Morgan Rogers.

Mikel Arteta had been eyeing Rogers and the club were understood to be preparing a bid for the England international.



However, London rivals Chelsea swooped in to sign him for a record-breaking £117million last week.

It leaves Arsenal still searching for a big-money arrival, with a move for Vini Jr. now not expected to materialise.

The Gunners have already signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge as a replacement for Leandro Trossard, who joined Besiktas.

They have also brought in goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer and signed Piero Hincapie on a permanent deal.

Sports.title: Stadium still a building site just weeks before it’s due to host European game
Sports.content:
Stadium still a building site just weeks before it’s due to host European game

Getafe face a race against time to get their stadium ready to host European matches, with major reconstruction works still incomplete.

The Spanish side are set to take part in the Conference League play-offs in a matter of weeks, having qualified after finishing seventh in LaLiga last season.

3 Entire stands at the Estadio Coliseum look largely incomplete, with just weeks until Getafe's Conference League opener Credit: Instagram / getafecf

But with their two-legged European showdown set to take place in late August, their Estadio Coliseum home still looks a way off being fit to host games.

Getafe have been playing their home games at a reduced capacity since redevelopment works on the ground started in June last year.

Their revamp has stepped up over the summer, as club bosses look to increase the venue by 2,000 seats to a 18,500 capacity, and with a roof covering every stand

The project isn't due to be complete for another 18 months, meaning it won't be ready by the start of the new season.

However, construction chiefs now have a new deadline to meet, as they are now scrambling to ensure the stadium will meet UEFA regulations in time for Getafe's Conference League clash.

European football‘s governing body sets out regulations on floodlighting, media infrastructure, hospitality areas and various other facilities for a venue to be allowed to host UEFA-sanctioned matches.

And the Estadio Coliseum could struggle to satisfy all of their demands in the coming weeks, if footage shared online is anything to go by.

Work to be done

In a recent video shared on Getafe's official social media pages, construction work looks to be far from complete.

With the stadium still resembling a building site, the stand behind one of their goals only appears to have seating in its lower tier.

Further footage shows another stand being rebuilt, with cranes visible from above as the work remains ongoing.

3 Footage has shown Getafe’s home ground is still in the midst of major reconstruction works Credit: Instagram / getafecf

The exterior of the ground is also in the midst of reconstruction, with the outside of the stands being rebuilt surrounded by rubble.

Building equipment and trucks can be seen around the ground, while the video also shows construction staff continuing their work on the renovation project.

Solution snubbed

Getafe had been in touch with city rivals Atletico Madrid about the prospect of playing European home games at the Metropolitano, located roughly 16 miles from the Estadio Coliseum.

But they have instead decided to pursue their current project, and will look to get their home ground ready in time.

The next part of the stadium plans involve the demolition of the Tribuna Stand, which runs along the west side of the pitch.

This will put the two-tiered grandstand out of action for the start of the new season, while the North Stand will also be out of use until the end of the year as work remains ongoing.

3 The Estadio Coliseum will soon have its capacity increased to 18,500 seats Credit: Getty

However, the South and Lateral Stands are expected to be completed in time.

Founded in 1983, Getafe moved into the Estadio Coliseum 15 years later in 1998.

With Spanish giants Real Madrid and Atletico the city's dominant teams, Getafe's home ground is the third-biggest of Madrid's three LaLiga teams.

Real's Santiago Bernabeu comes out on top, boasting a 83,186 capacity, ahead of the Metropolitano Stadium, with Atleti's home able to host 70,000 spectators.

However, Getafe's ground does trump Rayo Vallecano, whose Vallecas Stadium has a capacity of 14,708.

And while the Estadio Coliseum faces a race to be fit for European football, Rayo have concerns of their own and will be redeveloping their ground after serious safety concerns were detected.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino could earn millions with ‘plans to sell stakes in World Cup’ as UEFA issues damning statement
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino could earn millions with ‘plans to sell stakes in World Cup’ as UEFA issues damning statement

Gianni Infantino is looking to sell World Cup stakes in a controversial move that could earn him millions, according to a report.

The FIFA president has spent a decade at the top of football's global governing body but looks set to cash in on it's biggest tournament.



4 Infantino is reportedly planning to sell World Cup stakes Credit: AFP

According to The Times, he plans to market stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

This would lead to the introduction of a new company that will be in charge of top competitions across men's and women's football.

The World Cup and Club World Cup would also come under control, and therefore expansion or more regular editions could materialise.



In addition, the plan is said to have been discussed with figures close to US president Donald Trump.

Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared is Trump's son-in-law, has been eyed as the primary investor candidate with the bank JP Morgan.



The plan would also see stakes worth around $20million (£15m) given to all of the 211 member associations involved with FIFA.

Once his last term as president concludes, which could be in 2031 at the earliest, Infantino would likely be the group's commissioner.



UEFA hit back at FIFA plans

Following the publication of The Times' article, the European football governing body released a statement to condemn the plan.

"This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said.

"UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

4 Infantino could be in line for millions should he proceed Credit: Getty



"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.

"None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

Infantino under the spotlight

The 2026 World Cup was yet another spectacle on the pitch, but a series of controversies off it overshadowed the tournament.

Infantino has been the subject of intense scrutiny for his relationship with Trump, even before the World Cup began.

Trump was awarded the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize during the group stage draw in December.



He was championed by the FIFA president for 'unwavering commitment' to world peace through 'notable leadership and action'.

4 Infantino and his relationship with Trump has been a hot topic Credit: Getty

During the 2026 World Cup, United States striker Folarin Balogun had his one-match ban for a red card suspended for a year.

talkSPORT revealed that Trump called Infantino to review the decision, the only one of its kind out of all the 15 red card decisions.



In response, The Norwegian FA have intended to make a formal complaint to FIFA's ethics committee over Trump's intervention.

The red card has also been linked with potential betting irregularities.

On Monday, it was reported that a US lawmaker has requested for Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee.

Rep. Jamie Raskin wants Infantino's relationship with Trump to be scrutinised and FIFA to provide all records of their contact with the politician.



4 The report has sparked more conflict between FIFA and UEFA Credit: Getty

Infantino has responded to the criticism aimed at him by accusing people of 'spreading hate'.

He called upon critics to instead 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match'.

FIFA pump in more money

A matter of hours after UEFA's statement, FIFA announced plans to give $10billion of funding on football development, subject to approval by FIFA member assocations.



Global football's governing body says this would be part of the newly-launched FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which is a "new FIFA-owned and controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA’s commercial and event operations."

FIFA Forward Enterprise is controlled by FIFA, as is exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions.

It says the enterprise would raise up to $4.2bn later this year to fund the wider FIFA Fast Forward Programme "based on an initial equity valuation of $20bn by carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests in FFE."

FIFA claims all net benefits will be reinvested back into football worldwide.

Sports.title: English National League star joins Spanish club in unique role two months after signing new deal
Sports.content:
English National League star joins Spanish club in unique role two months after signing new deal

National League outfit Worthing have surprised fans by revealing Sam Beard has left the club two months after signing a new deal.

The club's vice-captain has completed a move to CD Atlético de Marbella Paraíso, which includes an academy coaching role.



2 Worthing boss Adam Hinshelwood will now have to replace his vice-captain Credit: Getty

The 28-year-old has made 200 appearances across the National League and National League South during his career.

The former Dorking, Barnet, and Eastbourne Borough player is now heading to Marbella to join a newly-promoted fifth-tier side.

The left-back has followed in the footsteps of his father, Mark Beard, who had a spell at Spanish lower league side San Pedro after his stints at the likes of Millwall, Sheffield United, and Southend.



National League star joins Spanish club in player/coach role

Former Brighton & Hove Albion youngster Beard was an integral part of Worthing's promotion to the National League last season.

‘Beardy’ started eight out of the club's final nine matches as the Mackerel Men were crowned National League South champions.



His manager Adam Hinshelwood - father of Brighton player Jack - was delighted to tie Beard down to a fresh contract in May.

“Beardy signing is a massive boost for us,” the 42-year-old revealed.

“He was a big part of our success towards the end of the season and is a player that has National League experience, which is going to be vital for our squad.”



Beard himself added: “I’m buzzing to extend my stay another year and play for this club in the National League.”

2 Beard (left) has left England to pursue the opportunity abroad Credit: Getty

However, two months later, Worthing confirmed an agreement has been reached with Atlético de Marbella Paraíso for Beard's transfer.

The Reds also revealed that alongside representing the Albicelestes as a player, their No.3 'will also work as a coach in their academy systems, contributing to several teams and age groups.'



Having helped return fifth-tier football to the Sussex Transport Community Stadium, Beard's new team achieved an identical promotion at the end of last season.

The phoenix club, who were born from the now defunct CA Marbella in 2010, will compete in the Tercera Federación this season for the first time in their existence.

Worthing, meanwhile, have already signed a new full-back this summer after agreeing a deal to loan QPR talent Cory Adjetey-Brew.

He joins fellow Queens Park Rangers teenager Harvey Boddy in spending the 2026/27 campaign with Hinshelwood's side.

Sports.title: Chelsea midfielder picks up 12th injury since joining in £58million deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea midfielder picks up 12th injury since joining in £58million deal

Romeo Lavia missed Chelsea's pre-season opener after Xabi Alonso confirmed the midfielder suffered from hamstring discomfort.

The majority of the Blues squad got valuable minutes under their belts during a 6-4 pre-season victory over Western Sydney Wanderers.

3 Lavia hasn't completed a full game for Chelsea since arriving from Southampton Credit: Getty

However, the 22-year-old was not among those involved having struggled for fitness ever since arriving from Southampton three years ago.

Recurring hamstring issues have limited the youngster to just 21 appearances for the west London outfit. Lavia is yet to complete 90 minutes in Chelsea colours.

The same problems resurfaced ahead of a pre-season match on Tuesday at the Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Chelsea's new boss spoke on Lavia's status: "He felt something in the hamstring.

"Not a big thing. We are expecting him to be fit for Saturday, hopefully."

It is hoped that the player can return for the upcoming clash against Premier League rivals Tottenham Hotspur, which will also be played in Sydney.

However, Lavia's frustrating injury record may prompt the club to adopt a precautionary approach with him.

Prior to the match, Chelsea released a 'diary entry' from the player, reflecting on how he was feeling ahead of the new season.

He wrote: "We have all enjoyed working under the new manager, and he has great experience in the game.

"Pre-season so far has been about getting the basics in place to build on, because we want to have a great season.

3 Chelsea have spent over £200million in new signings since Alonso arrived Credit: Getty

"The manager was a great player, one of the best of his generation. You see that when he steps into a training session.

"He starts pinging balls around in a way only those who have played at the top level can. It’s a privilege to be working with him, especially as a midfielder.

"Personally, I’m feeling good. I did a lot of work with people at the club to ensure I was ready and could start pre-season strong once we got going.

"Now come the games, and we’re looking forward to getting out in front of the fans."

Meanwhile, Chelsea managed to navigate the contest with Western Sydney with no further injuries despite playing on a patchy pitch.

The venue had hosted three rugby league matches in the days leading up to the football clash.

3 Jorgensen has left Chelsea's pre-season tour amid growing transfer interest Credit: Getty

Lavia was not the only player absent from the travelling squad to not appear, with Filip Jorgensen, Jorrel Hato and Mamadou Sarr left out.

Jorgensen was on a flight back to Europe to finalise a transfer to the Blues' sister club, Strasbourg.

Meanwhile, Hato and Sarr were deemed too unfit to start and played no part in the match.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini confirmed as new Italy boss – three years after resigning
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini confirmed as new Italy boss – three years after resigning

Italy have named Roberto Mancini as their new manager just three years after he stepped down from the role.

Mancini begins his second spell in charge of his nation following a five-year tenure from 2018 through to 2023.

3 Mancini has been named Italy manager again after winning the Euros in his last stint Credit: Getty

He led Italy to glory at the delayed Euro 2020 tournament, with his side beating Gareth Southgate's England on penalties at Wembley.

However, the former Manchester City manager also failed to qualify for the 2022 World Cup during his first stint as boss.

In total, Mancini took charge of 58 games with Italy - winning 38 matches and losing on just eight occasions.

Italy's main Man

Now, he returns - having been revealed by talkSPORT as a candidate in April - replacing Genaro Gattuso, who departed after his side missed out on the World Cup too.

Pep Guardiola was the first choice to take over from Gattuso, but he turned an approach down, opening the door for Mancini.

But the 61-year-old's appointment comes amid controversy within the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), which led to two resignations.

Italian icon Paolo Maldini quit his role as technical director alongside his advisor Leonardo after Andrea Pirlo was removed from the running to become the country's new manager.

Pirlo looked set to replace Gattuso, but due to his connection to a Russian betting company, the federation's president, Giovanni Malago, didn't want to appoint him.

That angered Maldini, who has now stepped down, with Malago going on to appoint Mancini instead of Pirlo.

He confirmed on Tuesday: "Mancini is the coach. I believed that the best person ​to become head coach was Roberto Mancini."

3 FIGC president Malago confirmed Mancini's appointment on Tuesday Credit: AFP

Why did Mancini resign in 2023?

Mancini resigned as Italy manager following a disagreement with the ex-FIGC president, Gabriele Gravina.

He did go on to thank Gravina in his leaving statement, which explained that his decision to leave his job was his own.

But the Premier League-winning boss eventually ended up revealing more details when speaking to an Italian newspaper.

Mancini said to La Repubblica: “Gravina had been trying for a year to revolutionise my staff. I tried to tell him that at most he could add a couple of new faces, but he couldn’t take away two members of a group that works and had won.

"If anything, it should be me who decides to substitute a member of my staff.

“Gravina had for a while thought about things very differently from me. I was massacred purely for my decision. I wanted to send a signal to the President, he could’ve helped me if he had wanted to.”

3 Ranieri has replaced Maldini as technical director with Italy too Credit: Getty

Maldini replacement

As well as appointing Mancini, Italy have also replaced Maldini following his resignation as technical director.

Legendary Italian manager Claudio Ranieri has been handed the role, with Malago explaining his decision to bring him in.

"I needed someone with whom I could share the decision on the coach, because without that shared view my reasoning would ⁠have ​carried little weight," the FIGC president said.

"So consequently, today we have ​a new coach and a new technical director for Italy."

Ranieri's last managerial role was with Roma in Serie A in 2025, with the 74-year-old now taking a behind-the-scenes position.

Italy's first fixture with their new, experienced faces involved will be on September 25 as they face Turkey in the Nations League.

Sports.title: Banned Olympian vanishes before 28th birthday as heartbroken mother makes desperate plea for help
Sports.content:
Banned Olympian vanishes before 28th birthday as heartbroken mother makes desperate plea for help

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The family of a former Brazilian Olympian is asking for help after the long distance runner disappeared from their home.

Daniel Nascimento, a marathoner who competed at the delayed Tokyo Olympics in 2021, left his home in a suburb of Sao Paulo on June 19 and has not returned since, according to an Instagram post from his mother.

The post - which his mother, Valdirene de Paula Ferreira, posted on Monday - asked for information regarding his whereabouts.

'His name is Daniel Nascimento. Better known [by the nickname] Armero,' she wrote in Portuguese.

'He was a marathon runner (he presents [with] psychological issues).'

According to Ferreira, her son left home in Paraguacu Paulista around 7:00pm on June 19 with a black backpack.

Brazilian marathoner Daniel Nascimento has disappeared, according to his mother

Nascimento (L) was living at home after being banned from competing for five years after testing positive for multiple forms of steroids before the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris

Nascimento's best achievement was a third-place finish in the 2022 Seoul Marathon. He also briefly led the New York City Marathon (above) that same year before he collapsed in the heat.

He had been under her care after he was banned from competition for five years beginning in May 2025, according to The Sun.

The family only formally reported his disappearance to the authorities on Monday - the day before Nascimento's 28th birthday.

Ferreira pleaded for any helpful information, and even listed her phone number to her followers and beyond.

'I would go to work and he would come with me. He was always a good boy,' she reportedly said. 'Sometimes I used to take him out for a run.

'He would do some training sessions in secret in the middle of the sugarcane fields. I think he really missed the routine of being an athlete.

'A thousand things go through your mind as a mother. I think I've lost about 10 kilos. Daniel's siblings are also very worried. We just want him to show up.'

Nascimento is the fastest marathoner in South America, but was banned for competing for five years after he tested positive for three different steroids a month before the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris. The ban took him out of those games as well as the upcoming Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

His biggest accomplishment was finishing third in the 2022 Seoul Marathon, running a 2:04:51. That year, he also led the New York City Marathon for over 20 miles before collapsing due to exhaustion on a hot race day.

Sports.title: Man City's forgotten man Kalvin Phillips is set for ANOTHER loan move after being left out of Man City squad for Asia tour - with injured Jack Grealish also absent
Sports.content:
Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City's squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42 million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

The 30-year-old former England international was desperate to make an impact, but his lack of games in recent seasons and subsequent shortage of match sharpness put him at a physical disadvantage.

The 31-cap international previously had loan spells with West Ham and Ipswich in the Premier League before linking up with Sheffield United in January.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday



Including his loan moves, he has made a total of 46 league appearances since joining City almost four years ago.

Talking to BBC Radio Sheffield towards the end of the season, Wilder said: 'He'll have a lot of people still after him. We've brought a really good pro in. He was unlucky with his injury and he's not played as much as he wanted to play.

MAN CITY TOUR SQUAD

Goalkeepers Gianluigi Donnarumma, Marcus Bettinelli, Max Chabot, Jack Wint. Defenders Rayan Ait-Nouri, Max Alleyne, Kaden Braithwaite, Josko Gvardiol, Matty Henderson-Hall, Abdukodir Khusanov, Rico Lewis, Stephen Mfuni, Vitor Reis. Midfielders Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Jaden Heskey, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Monga, Divine Mukasa, Nico Gonzalez, Xavier Parker, Tijjani Reijnders, Floyd Samba, Antoine Semenyo, Savinho. Forwards Mahamadou Sangare, Divin Mubama, Ryan McAidoo.

'I spoke to him and said we'd love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club if that is a possibility.

'He certainly ticks the box in terms of personality and characteristics, off the pitch and on it. If there's an opportunity I'm sure we'll try and explore that one.'

Jack Grealish has also been left out of City's pre-season tour as he continues his rehabilitation and individual training programme.

Grealish joined Everton on loan at the beginning of last season and his time with the Toffees got off to the perfect start as he notched two goals and six assists during the early months of the season.

But in January the attacker suffered a stress fracture during a game against his former club Aston Villa, which required surgery.

The injury marked the end of Grealish's season – and thereby killed his World Cup hopes - and he stayed at the Hill Dickinson club until the end of the season to undergo his rehabilitation.

He has since returned to City, posting a picture of himself on the grass last week with the caption: 'Nice to see everyone, am nearly there! Hopefully not long now till back training for good'.

There has been interest from Saudi Arabia - and Everton are also aware of his situation - but a decision on his future looks likely to come later in the window.

Savinho also wants to push through his move to Tottenham but City maintain his valuation has not been met and would want a replacement before they allow the 22-year-old to leave.

Sources at Tottenham indicate City's valuation has changed since initial talks.

City have considered the likes of Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG and Chelsea's Pedro Neto as potential wing additions.

Sports.title: Real Madrid to hold contract talks with Arsenal target Vinicius Jr as transfer saga takes a new twist: Club expect Brazilian star to STAY despite stand-off as Jose Mourinho makes stance clear
Sports.content:
Real Madrid to hold contract talks with Arsenal target Vinicius Jr as transfer saga takes a new twist: Club expect Brazilian star to STAY despite stand-off as Jose Mourinho makes stance clear

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Real Madrid will hold talks with the agents of Vinicius Jr this week as they try to find common ground on a new contract.

Arsenal remain attentive to developments after posting their interest in the potential blockbuster signing of the 26-year-old should the opportunity arise for what they recognise would be an expensive transaction.

Jose Mourinho wants Vinicius Jr to stay and Madrid are underlining they value the winger highly, but he has still to agree new terms and has one year remaining on contract.

Mourinho faced media on Tuesday as Madrid ran out 4-1 winners in a friendly over Leganes, but there were no bold statements as the Spanish media expect the club to keep one of their prized assets.

Madrid and his representatives are due to meet this week with the intention of making progress on a new long-term deal.

Mourinho has telephoned Vini Jr and is understood to have told him he wants him to stay.

Real Madrid are set to hold contract talks with Vinicius Jr, with Arsenal still interested

Madrid are still in the throes of agreeing a fee with RB Leipzig for winger Yan Diomande but the Ivory Coast international is set on moving to Santiago Bernabeu.

Some Arsenal insiders fear their efforts are futile but others want to continue to press in case Madrid fail to reach an agreement.

Meanwhile, Newcastle maintain they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing an offer around £70million for Vinicius Jr's compatriot but proposals have come through his agent so far.

Newcastle maintain he is not for sale but manager Eddie Howe admitted last weekend he was unsure where his captain's future lies.

Sports.content:
Newcastle insist Arsenal have NOT made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap... and Ajax want return for West Ham's Edson Alvarez: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Stones set for Inter medical

Inter Milan are expecting John Stones to undergo a medical on Thursday is ahead of his move to Italy.

The England international and his representatives are finalising terms over a free transfer and a two-year deal.

The 32-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester City and Inter are progressing in talks for Christian Romero from Spurs also.

Meanwhile, Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile and West Ham's Jean-Clair Todibo are on Napoli's list as the Serie A side work on signing a new centre back.

John Stones is set for a medical at Inter Milan as he prepares to join on a free transfer

Phillips edges closer to Blades return

Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City’s squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old - who has two years left on his contract - despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

Manchester City's Kalvin Phillips is on the verge of re-joining Championship Sheffield United

Black Cats zero in on Methalie

Sunderland are continuing talks over a potential £26million deal for left-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, the France Under 21 international defender, who can also operate as a centre-back, emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle United.

But Regis Le Bris is hopeful Sunderland can bring him in on a five-year contract for what would be a record sale for Toulouse.

Dayann Methalie (right) emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle

Forest putting out feelers for Famalicao's Sa

Nottingham Forest are in talks to sign Portuguese attacking midfielder Gustavo Sa from Famalicao.

The 21-year-old was a target for Saudi Arabian clubs earlier in the year and West Ham this summer but Forest may now sign him and then send on loan to Olympiacos.

Sa was the captain of Famalicao last season, scoring four goals and claiming two assists from 34 appearances.

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraes wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City
