World.title: Sea Floods Stari Grad on Hvar for the Third Time in Just 10 Days
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – The sea has created floods in Stari Grad on the island of Hvar for the third time in just 10 days due to repeated meteotsunamis.

Index reports that visitors and residents of Stari Grad on the island of Hvar have once again found themselves dealing with flooded streets after the sea overflowed onto the town’s waterfront, marking the third such event in just ten days. The repeated flooding has drawn attention to increasingly unusual sea level fluctuations affecting parts of Croatia’s coastline and islands.

Videos shared by residents showed seawater spilling over the promenade and into the historic centre, covering streets and public spaces before gradually receding. Although the flooding caused disruption, there were no reports of serious injuries or major structural damage.

According to meteorologists, the flooding was not caused by rainfall but by a combination of low atmospheric pressure, strong southerly winds and elevated sea levels. These conditions created what is known as a storm surge, pushing large volumes of seawater onto the shoreline and into low-lying coastal areas.

The phenomenon has affected Stari Grad several times over the past two weeks, with each event occurring under similar weather conditions. Locals say the repeated flooding has become a growing concern, particularly for businesses and residents along the waterfront who have had to repeatedly clear seawater from their properties.

Experts note that enclosed bays and historic harbour towns such as Stari Grad are especially vulnerable to this type of coastal flooding. When strong winds coincide with low air pressure, sea levels can temporarily rise enough to overwhelm quays, promenades and streets built just above normal sea level.

As weather conditions improved, the seawater gradually retreated and life returned to normal. However, the latest flooding serves as another reminder of how quickly changing weather patterns can impact Croatia’s coastal communities, with residents hoping calmer conditions will prevent another repeat in the coming days.

World.title: Sveti Ivan Beach: The Hidden Paradise That Requires a 50-Minute Hike
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – The entire island of Cres is stunning, but Sveti Ivan beach takes it a step further. If we’re being honest, it takes it many steps further, as a 50-minute hike is needed to reach this hidden paradise. Trust us, it’s so worth it.

Hidden beneath the ancient hilltop village of Lubenice on the island of Cres lies one of Croatia’s most spectacular beaches, Sveti Ivan beach. Putni kofer reveals that it is best known for its white pebbles, crystal-clear waters and particularly dramatic surroundings. It is very often considered one of the most beautiful beaches on the Croatian coast (and that’s a challenging title to receive in itself).

The beach sits in a secluded bay beneath the historic settlement of Lubenice, which is perched high on a cliff overlooking the Adriatic. Surrounded by steep rocks and untouched nature, Sveti Ivan offers the kind of peaceful atmosphere that is becoming increasingly rare on the Croatian coast.

Part of what keeps this beach so special is also what makes it difficult to reach. Visitors who choose to walk from Lubenice must follow a steep trail that takes around 50 minutes downhill, and the return journey can be even more challenging, especially during the intense summer heat. Proper footwear and enough water are essential, and we’d go as far as to discourage anyone doing this during the height of summer.

Because of the demanding access, even during the height of summer Sveti Ivan usually avoids the large crowds found at many other Croatian beaches. Those who make the journey are rewarded with incredible views, peaceful surroundings and some of the clearest waters on the Adriatic.

The beach can also be reached by sea, either with a private boat, organised excursion or water taxi. Nearby is another natural attraction, Plava Grota, a sea cave where sunlight creates beautiful blue reflections inside the cave.

Above the beach sits Lubenice, one of the oldest settlements on the Croatian islands. Located on a 378-metre-high cliff, the village has a history stretching back more than 4,000 years, with archaeological remains from the Bronze and Iron Ages found in the surrounding area.

Once one of Cres’ most important settlements, Lubenice is now home to only two permanent residents. However, during the summer months, visitors arrive to explore its ancient stone streets, admire the views and discover one of Croatia’s most breathtaking beaches down below.

World.title: Should Croatia Charge Tourists Who Need Emergency Help After Excessive Drinking?
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – Should Croatia be charging tourists who take it too far and require emergency medical help after excessive drinking or even illicit drug use?

Every single summer, Split in particular faces the same old problem, and that is tourists being found unconscious on city streets after heavy nights of drinking, with emergency services called to help them. The issue has sparked a debate over whether people who put themselves in danger through excessive alcohol consumption should contribute to the cost of medical interventions.

over 50 calls because of alcohol in june alone

During June alone, the Split-Dalmatia County Emergency Medical Service recorded more than 50 calls related to alcohol intoxication. Lukrecija Zderic reveals for Index that medical teams treated 44 people, while eight people were no longer at the location when emergency crews arrived. Among those who received help were also two minors.

Many of these cases involve young foreign tourists visiting Split during the summer season. Locals say it has become common to find intoxicated visitors lying on streets in the early morning hours after nights out and organised pub crawl tours.

The question now being raised is whether tourists who end up needing emergency medical assistance because of extreme alcohol consumption should help cover the cost. Some European countries already charge part of the expense in similar situations, but Croatia currently does not have such a system.

an abuse of already thin resources

Croatia’s emergency services are required to help anyone whose health is at risk, regardless of how the situation happened. However, every intervention requires medical staff, vehicles and resources.

The Croatian Health Insurance Fund explained that emergency medical teams are funded through contracted healthcare costs. A single emergency team consisting of a doctor, nurse and driver represents a significant annual expense for the healthcare system.

For foreign visitors, the final bill depends on their insurance situation. Tourists from EU countries, the European Economic Area and Switzerland with valid European Health Insurance Cards have their costs covered through international healthcare agreements. Visitors from countries without such agreements may have to pay themselves unless they have travel insurance.

irresponsible behaviour should face consequences

However, if a tourist leaves Croatia without paying a medical bill, the unpaid cost can ultimately fall on Croatian public funds. This means taxpayers may end up covering expenses that were never recovered.The debate comes as Split continues to balance the benefits of being one of Croatia’s most popular tourist destinations with the challenges that come from large numbers of visitors, particularly during the peak summer months.

As tourism grows, Croatia faces an ongoing question: should irresponsible behaviour surrounding alcohol and drug use that requires emergency medical intervention come with a financial consequence?

World.title: Estonian women's épée team narrowly miss world title, take silver
World.content:
Estonia's women's épée foursome took silver at the World Championships in Hong Kong after going down to Olympic champions Italy by just one point, in the final.

The last time the women's épée team reached the World Championship final was nearly a decade ago, in 2017. That time, the team defeated China to take gold.

After a disappointing run in the individual women's épée event late last week and over the weekend, the seventh-seeded women's épée foursome, consisting of Veronika Zuikova, reigning European champion Katrina Lehis, and two veterans from the 2017 final, Julia Beljajeva and Irina Embrich, went all the way to the final to narrowly lose 31–30 to the Italians.

Lehis was crowned European champion last month. Three of the four (Lehis, Beljajeva, and Embrich) were part of the team which took gold at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), while Beljajeva and Embrich were in the 2017 final, which Estonia won. Lehis also took bronze at the individual event in Tokyo.

Progress to the final

The team first faced Romania in the round of 32. They claimed a 36–25 victory in that match.

Katrina Lehis Source: FIE - International Fencing Federation

Next up came Canada, which Estonia cruised past with a 45–25 victory; Estonia lost just one of the nine individual bouts in that round.

In the quarterfinals, Estonia took on reigning world champions and Paris Olympic silver medalists France, who had defeated Chinese Taipei 45–18 and Israel 45–39.

Estonia made a superb start as Beljajeva blanked Alexandra Louis Marie von Kerssenbrock 5–0, Embrich scored the first two touches of her bout to give Estonia a 9–2 lead, and Lehis then defeated Marie-Florence Candassamy 4–2. After Beljajeva's touch in the fifth bout, the Estonians had stretched their lead to 19–7, and their advantage remained at at least 10 touches throughout. Embrich's victory over Candassamy extended Estonia's lead to 30–17.

The French attacked aggressively in the final two bouts. Von Kerssenbrock edged Lehis 9–8, and France's fourth team member, Auriane Mallo-Breton, beat Beljajeva 8–7, but Estonia's lead held up and the team advanced to the semifinals with a 45–34 win.

In the semifinals, the Estonian women faced Hungary, European Championship silver medalists three times over the past four years. Hungary had beaten the U.S. 43–38 in their quarterfinal.

Lehis beat top fencer Blanka Nagy 7–4 in the second bout, while Beljajeva again excelled, defeating the youngest member of the Hungarian team 4–1 to give Estonia a 14–9 overall lead after the fourth bout.

Estonia's Veronika Zuikova , Katrina Lehis, Julia Beljajeva and Irina Embrich took silver in the FIE World Championships in Hong Kong . Source: FIE/Bizzi Team

Embrich briefly found herself in trouble against Nagy, 27 years her junior, but then scored three consecutive touches. After Beljajeva's 3–2 victory over Lili Buki, Lehis entered the final bout holding a three-touch lead against Hungary's top fencer, Eszter Muhari. Lehis withstood the attacks of the Paris Olympic bronze medalist, won the bout 15–12, and sent Estonia into the final with a 42–34 overall victory.

Italy, who took olympic gold in Paris two years ago, edged South Korea 45–44 in a thrilling semifinal to set up the showdown with Estonia.

The final

The final in Hong Kong started at 3 p.m. Estonian time Tuesday.

Alberta Santuccio defeated Beljajeva 2–0 in the opening bout, and Estonia spent the rest of the final chasing the deficit, which got as narrow as one point early on in the tournament as Beljajeva's victory in her second bout, when things were 11–10 in the Italians' favor. Lehis however then lost 4–0 down to Giulia Rizzi in the sixth bout, allowing the olympic champions to extend their lead to six touches. Embrich and Beljajeva together managed to pull Estonia one touch closer, leaving Lehis to begin the final bout trailing 24–19.

While Lehis expertly put her Italian opponent under pressure and gradually reduced Estonia's deficit – With 40 seconds remaining, Lehis closed to within a single touch, but there was simply too little time left. The final seconds featured five consecutive double touches, leaving Italy to claim a narrow 31–30 victory.

Editor's note: This piece was updated to include the final result.

World.title: Photos: Demolition begins at Tallinn's Eesti Näitused expo center
World.content:
Demolition has begun at Tallinn's former Eesti Näitused expo center, where a new residential development is planned along Pirita tee.

The last trade fair at the center was held in mid-June.

Mait Allas, CEO of real estate developer Metro Capital, told ERR that demolition of the Soviet-era exposition halls, which began Tuesday, is expected to take two to three months.

Metro Capital plans to begin construction of Marienberg Quarter on the nearly 7-hectare site in 2028, with plans including apartment buildings, a kindergarten, a pedestrian boulevard and green spaces.

Some nearby residents previously challenged the plans in court, but those disputes have since been resolved, and the developer says it hopes to reach agreements with neighbors going forward.

The project timeline now depends partly on approval of the site's zoning plan, which is nearing completion. Allas said he hopes it will be approved this fall, allowing design work to begin soon after.

World.title: Estonian firefighters to help put out wildfires in Italy
World.content:
Estonia's Rescue Services Agency will send firefighters to Italy to support local efforts in putting out wildfires, Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) has said.

France, Spain, northern Portugal, and northern Italy have been hit hardest by the current wildfires in Southern Europe.

Tsahkna said that the Estonian Rescue Services Agency wildfire firefighting team will join local response efforts in Sardinia, Italy, to fight the fires.

"We are deeply grateful to every firefighter and emergency responder risking so much to protect lives, homes and nature," he said in a statement on social media.

"These devastating wildfires remind us that strengthening our resilience, caring for our environment and preparing for a changing climate is ultimately about protecting people, their homes and the places they cherish," he added.

My heart goes out to everyone affected by the devastating wildfires across Southern Europe.

World.title: Prosecutor's Office puts money from conditionally terminated cases into a lottery pool
World.content:
Financial obligations imposed in Estonian criminal cases ended through conditional termination used to have to be paid into the state treasury, but now that money may, through a lottery, end up with NGOs. Last week, two local sports clubs became €6000 richer.

Previously, in cases ended with conditional termination, the Prosecutor's Office could direct the person entering into the agreement to perform community service or require them to pay a set amount into state revenues.

The Prosecutor's Office suspected MP Tõnis Mölder of accepting a bribe and attempted to have his parliamentary immunity removed. Although the Riigikogu did not vote in favor of that, proceedings continued with the two alleged bribe givers and the intermediary.

Last week it emerged that the cases of those two individuals ended with conditional termination, and both men had to pay €6000 for that purpose. However, the money did not go to the state treasury but instead to two sports clubs — the Järvamaa Sports Association and Sakala Biathlon.

Kristjan Lill Autor/allikas: ERR/Vikerraadio

Kristjan Lill, senior prosecutor at the Northern District Prosecutor's Office, said in an interview that since 2024 it has been possible to direct the financial obligation imposed under conditional termination to targeted use in the public interest.

According to Lill, the recipients may be non‑profit organizations, foundations, and religious associations that are listed by the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA) as eligible for income‑tax benefits. The prosecutor must propose such a "donation."

When making the selection, the prosecutor can narrow the possible choices based on several criteria, with the final selection determined by lottery.

"Whether to choose organizations operating across Estonia or, from the perspective of the Viru District Prosecutor's Office, perhaps organizations in Ida‑Virumaa and Lääne‑Virumaa," Lill said, adding that the selection can also be made by field of activity. For example, the list includes culture, children, animals, and sports, as well as a separate category for supporting Ukraine.

Lill said NGOs and foundations should not expect money to start flowing toward them.

"It's more like a lottery, and certainly not everyone will get money. In the EMTA's list — I may be mistaken — there are between 1000 and 2000 organizations."

As an interesting detail, Lill pointed out that if a suspect or accused person accepts such an obligation and pays the amount accordingly, they can deduct the donation as tax‑exempt income up to €8400.

World.title: Estonian schools struggle to fill math and primary‑class teaching jobs
World.content:
Schools are looking most actively — through public job postings — for mathematics teachers and primary‑class teachers, but English teachers are also in very high demand. The largest number of vacancies is in Tallinn and Harju County, but teachers are frequently missing in Lääne‑Virumaa and Tartu County as well.

In the Õpetajate Leht job listings, schools are seeking 147 education workers — 134 teachers and 13 special‑education or support staff.

There are 92 active postings in total. Although some advertised positions may already be filled, the data provides a good overview of which types of teachers are most needed in which municipalities.

Olga Selištševa, director of Tallinn Tõnismäe State High School, which is looking for four teachers, said the high demand is nothing new. "It was the same last year and the year before. It's an annual situation," she said.

According to Selištševa, the large number of people aspiring to become teachers may give the impression that many new teachers are entering schools, but in reality most who enroll in teacher‑training programs are already working in schools and simply want to obtain the qualification.

"New people aren't coming, and that's the problem," she said.

Tallinn Avatud Kool opened on September 1 in Tallinn, one of two new schools opening in the capital this year. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

By county, Harju County has the most vacancies, with 32 job postings. Lääne‑Virumaa is looking for 12 education workers, and Tartu County for 10.

Pärnu County and Järva County each have five openings, Ida‑Virumaa four, and Jõgeva, Põlva, and Valga counties three each. Rapla, Viljandi, and Võru counties each have two, and Lääne County has one vacancy.

By position type, the largest number of postings are for primary‑class teachers, with 34 vacancies. Among subject teachers, mathematics teachers are most sought after, with 26 postings.

Schools are looking for 19 English teachers and 15 music teachers. There are 11 postings for Estonian language and literature teachers, and four for Estonian language teachers.

Physics teachers are needed for eight positions and chemistry teachers for four, plus one combined physics‑or‑chemistry posting.

Among support specialists and positions related to teaching students with special needs, the most vacancies are for speech therapists, who are sought by 19 institutions.

In many cases, schools need more than one new teacher.

World.title: Infrastructure in Estonia surges while apartment construction falters
World.content:
Apartment building in Estonia is currently sluggish, while infrastructure is booming, says Tarmo Pohlak, board member of the construction company Nordecon.

Pohlak says that the many construction cranes currently visible in central Tallinn represent only the tip of the iceberg, and the decisions to build those buildings were often made long ago.

At the same time, major infrastructure projects are underway in Estonia: 45 kilometers of 2+2 road are being built on the Tallinn–Pärnu highway, and part of the Tallinn–Tartu highway is also out to tender.

Construction of Rail Baltic is ongoing as well, though it is not very visible to ordinary people in the cityscape. Based on current knowledge, Estonia will complete its entire section up to Ikla on the Latvian border, and the pace will be very fast until 2030. "There are very large volumes of concrete, earthworks and other materials," Pohlak said.

According to him, Nordecon is also building several national defense facilities deep in the forests, where the work volumes are quite large.

Pohlak says the economy is currently highly volatile, yet construction companies are required to adhere to fixed prices. "Someone made the comparison that if Eesti Pank says it cannot produce very precise forecasts, then construction companies, when submitting bids, must be able to foresee everything and factor it into their price."

"Reedene intervjuu": Tarmo Pohlak Autor/allikas: Ken Mürk/ERR

In the private sector, Nordecon is currently building two hotels — one in Viljandi and the other on the shore of Lake Peipus. "Both entrepreneurs have taken a big risk, and we are happy to build."

But when it comes to apartment construction, current volumes are incomparably smaller than before the COVID pandemic.

Developing commercial real estate is also difficult at the moment. "You have to believe you will have clients, or in the case of an office building, you must know who you are building it for. You have to secure an anchor tenant. Entrepreneur Urmas Sõõrumaa signed a contract with SEB Bank, which is a very large anchor, and thanks to that the major Talsinki Quarter project went ahead. It is a very large private investment in central Tallinn, but without the SEB contract, that plot would be silent today," Pohlak noted.

The new 'Talsinki' retail and residential area in central Tallinn. Source: Talsinki arhitektuuri loovad arhitektuuribürood Arhitekt 11 ja HGA, maastikuarhitektuuri autor on TajuRuum. Sisearhitektuuri kujundavad studio ARGUS (kodud) ja LÄVI (bürood). Ehitab Bildgren Ehitus.

The state is improving infrastructure, but practically no new large state building projects are coming, Pohlak said. The only known project is the Siuru Cultural Center in Tartu. There are some schools and kindergartens, but from the builder's perspective these are relatively small.

Pohlak recalled that in spring 2022, at the start of the war in Ukraine, a materials shortage emerged reminiscent of Soviet times. "I was on the client side then, walking around the site. One wall was insulated with one type of mineral wool, another with a different type, and a third with a third type. If you asked the main contractor why, they used whatever they could get at that moment. If nothing was available, work stopped. The price of rebar doubled or tripled overnight."

According to Pohlak, the building sector adapted to the situation, but now there are new problems. The situation in the Strait of Hormuz pushes oil and gas prices up and down. Many construction materials — and transport — are tied to oil and gas prices.

Pohlak noted that if all Ukrainian construction workers were to leave Estonia, the impact would be catastrophic. "Without foreign labor it would be very difficult, because there are not enough workers. And they are very capable."

Cranes building the Rail Baltica terminal in Tallinn. Source: Mait Ots/ERR

World.title: Ida-Viru County seeks tourism rebrand beyond Soviet-era 'ghost town' image
World.content:
Being adjacent to the eastern border and its distance from Tallinn mean Ida-Viru County has long been somewhat off the beaten track, attracting more niche types of tourism than other parts of the country.

One classic example of this is the former mining town of Viivikonna, famed for being a ghost town, though there are people living there again nowadays.

Local residents are often keen to move away from the old Soviet tag and embrace something new.

"We want to turn [Viivikonna] back into a holiday destination, with beautiful backyards. Perhaps in the future it could become an example of how to turn an ugly town into a beautiful settlement," Priit Orav, who has worked as a tour guide in the area for around 25 years, suggested.

Viivikonna as it is now has, thanks to its abandoned and eerie nature, long been a popular destination for visitors, tourists, and even filmmakers exploring new locations.

Ruined building in Viivikonna. Source: Chris Feichtner/Flickr

"I think there is already enough material about it on YouTube, and filmmakers from all over the world have been there. Now I think it is time to draw a line under it. We need to move on from this Soviet nostalgia. Right next door, beautiful private homes have been built or old ones have been renovated, and everything is already beginning to take on a European appearance," Orav explained, talking to "Vikerhommik".

The transformation process is already underway, and the larger buildings have largely been demolished, leaving only the former schoolhouse and a few smaller residential buildings.

These latter buildings are often being used as homes nowadays in any case, Orav noted. "What is left are smaller houses that were once built for four families. They have become homes for one or two families, with beautiful gardens. People do care about their surroundings."

In the quarter of a century Orav has worked as a guide in Viivikonna, he has conducted around 100 tours of the so-called ghost town, and so has seen the transformation at first hand. "I have seen this change and I have also seen the reaction of the local residents. They have for a long time been tired of the fact that so many people go there, and that the place has attracted the attention of social media around the world," he said.

The same can be said of the surrounding area. "I hope this place will develop into a quiet, nice settlement with low-density housing. Just 10 kilometers away is Sillamäe, which has also become very beautiful nowadays," Orav added.

The center of Sillamäe is an example of typical Stalinist architecture. Source: Visit Estonia/ Tauri Taal.

He also often conducts tours of Sillamäe, a nearby port town with notable neoclassical architecture dating mostly to the Stalinist era. "Of course, it has a Russian or Soviet 'accent', but that is exactly what people come to see, because there is no other city like it in Estonia. Now we just have to wait for the local residents of Sillamäe to grasp that the old town of Sillamäe is an attraction, and that the buildings and exterior façades ultimately need to be restored."

Other highlights include the beach at Narva-Jõesuu, downstream from Narva and a resort town. It is very difficult to find anything similar to Narva-Jõesuu elsewhere, Orav said, also bringing out the Aidu quarry, where a versatile water sports center has been established, as characterizing a new emerging trend.

"The Kiviõli ash hills have found their place, but the new rowing channel at Aidu and everything else around it, as well as the underground mine in Kohtla-Nõmme, are things that only we have; there is nothing like them elsewhere in Estonia."

Kiviõli hosts a notable motocross circuit, skiing can be done on some of the artificial slopes left over from mine tailings, and the forests of Ida-Viru County are home to a population of Siberian Flying Squirrels.

Ultimately what makes Ida-Viru County a special tourism destination is its natural beauty: Its vast array of rivers, lakes, the sea, forests, bogs, and wetlands, Orav concluded.

World.title: New ambassador to the US: I'm ready to run in presidential elections
World.content:
Incoming Estonian ambassador to the United States Hannes Hanso has said he would be willing to be a candidate at September's Estonian presidential elections, if asked.

Hanso, 54, until recently Estonia's ambassador to China, said he would make a good president if elected, adding more than one party has floated the idea.

"It is true that two or three parties have discussed my possible candidacy in various formats. Also in a broader circle. That is, in itself, a great honor for me," the newly appointed representative to Washington, told Vikerraadio's Uudis+ program Tuesday.

In response to the host's question about what his response would be if party leaders asked him to run for president, Hanso said: "What would I say? It would be tough for us to reorganize our family life once again, but I would definitely be ready. I have no doubt that I would be a good president of the republic."

Hanso noted his resume includes a stint as minister of defense (2015-2016). He has also served in local government, including as a mayor, and on local councils as well, and national politics as a past Riigikogu member, where he chaired the Riigikogu's foreign affairs and national defense committees at various times. He was also briefly an MEP (2019).

"If those are the experiences and competencies that are being sought, then as a citizen it would almost be irresponsible to say 'no,' if such a consensus could be built around me. To refuse to take on that responsibility. Then we would have to reshuffle our cards once again, and the children would also be very happy that they could finally live in Estonia again. In short, Hannes Hanso would not throw in the towel and would say 'yes'."

Hanso also said he does not like the situation which has emerged around Estonia's presidential election process and the upcoming election in particular.

Ballots being counted at the first round of the 2021 presidential election. Source: Erik Peinar, Chancellery of the Riigikogu

"The world is unstable and turbulent. We need some clarity, and people should be honest. If they have an ambition to become president, they should say so. Be a man and say it, or be a woman and say it: 'Yes, I am interested. I believe we all have a responsibility for these matters.' Standing behind a bush, hedging, or keeping the door open without saying anything – there is really no need for such fear. It is the greatest honor a person can have: to be the head of state, the country's leader."

Hanso was appointed Estonia's next ambassador to the U.S. in early June, replacing Kristjan Prikk, who is to become Estonia's ambassador to NATO later in the year. Hanso had been ambassador to Beijing up to his new appointment.

Hanso's declaration comes at a time when several other public figures have either been put forward by politicians as candidates, or declared their own interest in running. The first group includes Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, while former Defense League commander Riho Ühtegi is in the latter camp.

Estonia's presidents are elected by the Riigikogu in the first instance, with a majority of 68 at the 101-seat chamber needed, meaning cross-party support of coalition and opposition parties is required for a candidate to get voted in.

If three rounds of voting draw a blank, the process moves to the regional electoral college.

Nominations open for candidates on August 21, and close August 24. The Riigikogu voting rounds start on September 2.

Hanso was a member of the Social Democratic Party (SDE) from February 2009 until June 2019.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 526,000 bpd in May and June
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s average oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 526,470 barrels per day, compared to about 329,500 barrels per day in April, amid ongoing shipping and energy disruptions in the Gulf region.

The revenues generated from Iraqi oil exports saw an improvement over the last two months, supported by a relative increase in shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and the activation of alternative export routes.

Oil prices fluctuated, remaining high at around $100 per barrel during May before falling below that level in June.

The rising oil prices boosted Iraq’s export income in May and June 2026, when there were fears about supply constraints and increased Asian demand, notably from China and India.

Iraqi oil exports have been under growing strain since the beginning of March, following the suspension of loading operations at southern ports due to the US war against Iran, which had a direct impact on marine security in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO), Iraq’s total oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 32.11 million barrels, with a monthly average of over 16 million barrels.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

Experts believe that the current price levels of oil are likely to provide Baghdad with a better financial margin to mitigate some losses incurred from the significant decline in exports, even amidst ongoing security tensions in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Turkey on an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Tuesday, for an official visit following an invitation from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

Turkish media highlighted the significance of the visit, as it is expected to broaden constructive collaboration between the two countries, particularly in the areas of water, energy, security, and economic cooperation, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

In addition to trade, security cooperation, and combating terrorism, al-Zaidi will discuss establishing a cooperative water management entity based on shared interests, as well as scientific collaboration and investment in advanced technology, to serve the interests of both Iraq and Turkey.

Al-Zaidi is scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for an official visit, following his diplomatic trip to the Turkish capital, Ankara.

The trip is part of a larger regional diplomatic tour aiming to maintain regional balance and strengthen Iraq’s business connections.

The prime minister recently conducted high-level diplomatic visits to the United States on July 13 and Iran on July 23.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: US drone shot down in western Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An unknown drone, first claimed by Iranian official media IRIB as a US surveillance one, crashed within a residential complex near the Haditha Dam in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Iraqi police and security agencies later indicated that the drone’s origin remains unknown, according to Al-Jazeera.

The debris was discovered blazing in a residential compound near the Haditha Dam in Anbar.

Local police stated that there were no recorded injuries or civilian deaths as a result of the collision.

Iranian state media swiftly released images of the smoking debris, claiming it was a US drone shot down amid broader regional activity.

The incident took place during a night of broad military conflict in Iraq, which included many drone attacks and defensive responses.

At least four Iranian drones attacked targets northeast of the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil, sparking a huge defensive reaction, including over ten US jets and drones sent to inspect the skies.

Air defense systems were activated at Anbar’s Ain al-Asad Air Base in response to a drone strike.

Explosions, alleged suicide drones, and radar interruptions were also reported at Camp Taji, Balad Air Base, and Imam Ali Base in southern Iraq.

The US military has not publicly verified the loss of any aircraft in Anbar. Investigations into the model and operator of the crashed drone are still underway.

World.title: Al Zaidi: Iraq and Turkey can build a regional success story through economic integration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi said on Tuesday that the Middle East needs new success stories built on economic integration rather than conflict, arguing that Iraq and Turkey have the potential to create a model regional partnership through joint investment, infrastructure, and trade.

The remarks came in an article published by Turkey’s Anadolu Agency ahead of Al Zaidi’s official visit to Ankara, where he is expected to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and senior officials.

Al Zaidi said relations between Iraq and Turkey have traditionally focused on managing issues such as security, water resources, trade, and border crossings. However, he argued that regional changes require a more ambitious vision centered on economic cooperation.

He said Iraq has chosen a path of stability, reform, and development, prioritizing a stronger economy, an effective state, and balanced foreign relations that make regional cooperation a pillar of growth.

According to Al Zaidi, Turkey’s industrial base, strategic location, and expertise in infrastructure, energy, and transportation complement Iraq’s geographic position, creating an opportunity to establish one of the region’s most significant economic partnerships.

The prime minister highlighted the Development Road Project, describing it as more than an Iraqi initiative. He said the corridor could redefine economic connectivity in the Middle East by linking Gulf ports with Asian and European markets.

He added that the project would not only reduce shipping times but also create new cities, industrial zones, investment opportunities, and thousands of jobs, while establishing a new economic artery connecting ports to global markets.

Al Zaidi also stressed that security cooperation remains essential, saying Iraq’s and Turkey’s security are closely linked and require mutual respect for sovereignty as well as joint efforts to combat terrorism and organized crime.

On water issues, he said water is no longer simply a technical matter but a development challenge affecting millions of people. He called for a shared approach based on mutual interests, scientific cooperation, and investment in modern technologies to strengthen water and food security.

“The Middle East needs new success stories,” Al Zaidi wrote, adding that Iraq and Turkey can provide one if they move beyond traditional cooperation toward genuine economic integration.

He said every joint investment, factory, transport route, and energy project represents an investment in regional stability, arguing that lasting stability is built through shared projects rather than conflict.

Later on Tuesday, Al Zaidi departed for Ankara at the head of a high-level government delegation. According to the Prime Minister’s Office, the visit will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in the fields of economy, water, security, investment, and regional affairs.

The two sides are also expected to review the implementation of existing agreements and memoranda of understanding, while discussing progress on joint infrastructure projects, including the Development Road initiative.

World.title: Drone attack targets Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Drone attacks targeted the Khor Mor gas field in the northern Iraqi province of Sulaymaniyah in the early hours of Tuesday.

The attack on the field, which is Iraq’s largest gas field with reserves estimated at 8.2 trillion cubic feet, was part of a coordinated wave of suspected Iranian drone attacks against the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Iranian official media reported an attack on the gas field, which is operated by the UAE-based Pearl Consortium that includes Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum.

The gas field supplies the majority of the electricity in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to reports, the strikes were carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which targets Iranian Kurdish resistance groups and US interests in the region.

A few days ago, Iraqi Kurdistan’s Prime Minister Masoud Barzani stated that repeated security threats and drone attacks had caused energy companies to cut domestic output, seriously affecting the region’s electrical infrastructure.

The escalation takes place amid significant geopolitical challenges. On Monday, US President Donald Trump said he was ready to resume military action against Iran if diplomatic efforts to reach a nuclear deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz failed.

Trump stated that he has temporarily stopped military strikes against Iran to give negotiations a chance to work.

World.title: Iraq, Australia cooperate to sentence alleged drug trafficker to life imprisonment
World.content:
An Iraqi court has sentenced convicted drug trafficker Kazem Hamad to life imprisonment after finding him guilty of drug trafficking and links to transnational organized crime, in a case that involved close cooperation between Iraqi and Australian authorities.

The ruling marks a significant development in Iraq’s ongoing campaign against organized crime and narcotics trafficking.

In a statement issued on Monday, Iraq’s judiciary described Hamad as “one of the most wanted individuals by Iraqi and international courts.” According to the judiciary, Hamad was responsible for smuggling large quantities of heroin into both Iraq and Australia.

The statement also accused him of involvement with transnational criminal networks engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, kidnapping, extortion, and organized violence.

Australian authorities have identified Hamad as a key figure in Melbourne’s so-called “tobacco wars,” a violent conflict between organized crime groups competing for control of the illicit tobacco and vape market.

The turf war has been linked to more than 200 arson attacks, firebombings, and extortion incidents across the Australian city. Hamad was deported from Australia in 2023 and was arrested in Iraq in January 2026, where prosecutors charged him with smuggling narcotics into both countries.

The Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed earlier this year that it had provided operational information to support Iraq’s investigation. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in February that the agency would continue cooperating with Iraqi authorities while pursuing its own investigation into Hamad and his alleged criminal network under Operation Carmen.

Australian investigators have also linked Hamad to several serious crimes, including allegations that he played a role in the December 2024 firebombing of Melbourne’s Adass Israel Synagogue, according to Australian media reports.

The life sentence comes as Iraq continues to intensify its fight against drug trafficking and organized crime. Despite imposing some of the region’s toughest penalties, including life imprisonment and the death penalty for major narcotics offenses, Iraq has experienced a sharp rise in drug trafficking and addiction since 2003.

Officials say authorities have arrested thousands of suspects in recent years as part of nationwide anti-drug operations. Iraq was recently ranked third globally in combating narcotics at the World Police Summit in the United Arab Emirates, reflecting the country’s expanding efforts to dismantle trafficking networks.

World.title: 'Every possible measure must be taken': Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says no Indian seafarer should be caught in crossfire
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid escalating geopolitical tensions affecting key global shipping routes and posing risks to Indian sailors, shipping minister

Tuesday directed officials to ensure âno Indian seafarer finds himself caught in the crossfire of geopolitical conflictâ.

Safety of Indian mariners remains govtâs top priority, he said while chairing a high-level review meeting on the safety and welfare of Indian seafarers serving aboard merchant vessels in conflict-sensitive regions. The meeting was attended by officials from different departments and heads of Indian missions in Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Russia and Ukraine.

âNo Indian seafarer should find himself caught in the crossfire of geopolitical conflict.

Every possible measure must be taken to safeguard our seafarers, support their families and ensure timely assistance wherever required,â the minister said.

Meanwhile, on X, Forward Seamenâs Union of India (FSUI) claimed that AMIR1, currently at Ukrainian port Chornomorsk with 15 crew on board, including 13 Indian seafarers, was trapped in a âterrible and life-threatening situationâ.

It said, âRepeated drone and missile attacks are being attempted in the immediate vicinity of the vessel.





The crew is living under constant fear of a direct hit at any moment,â while appealing to authorities, shipowners, flag state, and govt to immediately secure their safety and arrange prompt repatriation.

During the meeting, officials reviewed the prevailing security situation, maritime developments and the preparedness of Indian diplomatic missions.

DG Shipping informed the minister that its 24x7 Seafarer Grievance and Assistance Cell remains fully operational.

It added that to strengthen preparedness, the maritime regulator has asked Recruitment and Placement Service Licensees (RPSLs) to conduct structured pre-departure orientation programmes to familiarise seafarers with operational conditions, security protocols and evolving geopolitical risks in deployment areas.

Recognising the psychological stress of prolonged deployment in volatile regions, Sonowal also directed officials to integrate mental health support into the seafarer welfare framework, including counselling services for seafarers and their families and greater transparency on operational risks before deployment.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Bus with Amarnath pilgrims slips into gorge, 39 hurt
World.content:
SRINAGAR: At least 39 Amarnath pilgrims, including 21 from Madhya Pradesh and 19 Rajasthan natives, were injured after their bus skidded off the road in Ganiwan in J&Kâs Ganderbal district and slipped into a 50-foot-deep gorge on Tuesday morning.

The fall was broken midway at around 25 feet by a house in a mountain hamlet below the road, preventing the vehicle from sliding further down the slope and averting a major tragedy, locals said.

The devotees were heading back after visiting the holy cave shrine. The vehicle was moving from Baltal towards Srinagar when the accident occurred around 7 am near Ranga Morh, prompting a multi-agency rescue operation. Residents said the house belonged to Din Mohammad, who was away grazing sheep with his family at the time.

J&K Police, CRPF, ITBP, health department and civil defence personnel rushed to the spot and launched a coordinated rescue operation, with assistance from locals. The injured were moved to SKIMS in Soura, Srinagar.

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited SKIMS, where doctors briefed him about the health condition of those injured. In an X post, Sinha said he instructed officials to ensure the best possible treatment for the hospitalised pilgrims and arrangements for their safe return upon recovery.





Health minister Sakeena Itoo also visited SKIMS and interacted with the injured pilgrims, assuring them of full govt support. She directed hospital authorities to monitor each patientâs condition and ensure round-the-clock availability of specialist doctors and essential healthcare services.

This year's Amarnath Yatra began on July 3. The 57-day annual pilgrimage will conclude on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan. As of July 26, more than 4,14,000 pilgrims had completed the annual pilgrimage and offered prayers at the holy cave shrine.

World.title: CBI files chargesheet against 13 accused in NEET-UG paper leak case; hearing tomorrow
World.content: NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Tuesday filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak case before the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi.The chargesheet, filed by the Economic Offences Wing of the CBI, will be placed before the special fast-track court constituted to hear paper leak cases on Wednesday.According to the agency, the case has been registered under Sections 315(5), 318(4), 61(2), 238 and 303(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, along with Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and Sections 3, 4, 5, 10 and 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.As per the information shared by ANI, the accused named in the chargesheet are Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal, Vikas Biwal, Subham Khairnar, Dhananjay Lokhande, Prahalad Kulkarni, Tejas Harshad Kumar, Dr Manoj Shirure, Shivraj Raghunath Motegaonkar, Manisha Waghmare, Manisha Mandhare, and Manisha Sanjay Hawaldar.All 13 accused are currently in judicial custody.The alleged leak of the NEET-UG examination paper triggered nationwide outrage and led to multiple investigations into irregularities in the conduct of the medical entrance examination.Dharmendra Pradhan also resigned on July 25 as Union education minister, following which the Cockroach Janta Party withdrew its 36-day agitation that had mobilised lakhs of people over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and the NEET paper leak.

World.title: After SC order, West Bengal govt says no action against NEET protesters, except those with criminal records
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Tuesday announced that it would not take any coercive action against students who participated in recent demonstrations over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue.

However, the BJP-led state government clarified that the relief would not apply to individuals with criminal antecedents.

The directions are in line with the Supreme Court's interim order earlier in the day, under which states can continue investigations into registered FIRs but cannot take coercive action against students who participated in protests, provided they have no criminal antecedents.

According to an official press release, one case had been registered in West Bengal in connection with the NEET (UG) paper leak protest issue and 16 people had been arrested as of 6 pm on July 26.

Earlier, two other BJP-led states, Bihar and Assam,

the withdrawal of cases and legal proceedings against all protesters involved in demonstrations over the alleged NEET (UG) examination irregularities.

In Maharashtra, another BJP-led state, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis

the state home department to issue orders for the withdrawal of cases registered against students who participated in the protests.





The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that led the main protests in Delhi, has warned of resuming its agitation if cases against all protesters are not withdrawn. The demand was among the conditions accepted by the Centre, following which the CJP called off its indefinite sit-in on July 25.

The CJP had been protesting at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since June 21.

World.title: Law on delayed birth registration to be more stringent; govt says birth certificate gives one legal identity
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A bill seeking to make the provision for delayed registration of births and deaths more stringent, is set to be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and shall require every birth or death reported to the registrar after two years of its occurrence, to be registered on only an order made by a judicial magistrate of the first class.

As per the statement of objects and reasons of The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the proposal to make the law more stringent is based on consultations held with the state/UT govts and other stakeholders and âwill encourage timely reporting of events of birth and deathâ.

It added that âthe registration of births and deaths is mandatory under the Act and the birth/death certificate issued after such registration, provides legal identity to an individualâ and âis admissible as evidence for the purpose of proving the birth and death of a personâ.

Birth certificate is also the key document for determining a person's citizenship status. It is one of the documents accepted during the special intensive revision (SIR) electoral roll, as a proof of citizenship.

The bill seeks to add sub-section 3A to Section 13, requiring any birth or death intimated to the registrar after two years of occurence, to be registered only on the order of a first-class judicial magistrate, âafter verifying the correctness of the birth or death and on payment of such fee as may be prescribedâ.





The existing Section 13(3) mandates that a birth or death, of which delayed information is shared with the registrar after one year but within two years of its occurrence, will be registered only on order of a district magistrate, sub-divisional magistrate or an executive magistrate authorised by the district magistrate and appointed under Section 14(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

The rules to implement Section 13(3A) â including determination of the prescribed fee for delayed registration â may be framed by the state govt, empowered under Section 30 to do so.

World.title: 13 Indians stranded aboard vessel in Ukraine amid repeated drone, missile attacks: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Thirteen Indian seafarers are among 15 crew members stranded on board a cargo vessel at Ukraine's Chornomorsk port, where repeated drone and missile attacks have placed the crew in what has been described as a "life-threatening situation", according to the Forward Seamen's Union of India (FSUI).

In an urgent appeal posted on X, the union said the vessel, MV AMIR1, remains docked at Chornomorsk while hostilities continue in the surrounding area.

"MV AMIR1, currently at Ukrainian port Chornomorsk with 15 crew on board, including 13 Indian seafarers, is trapped in a terrible and life-threatening situation," it said.

The union alleged that drone and missile attacks were being carried out in the immediate vicinity of the ship, leaving the crew in constant fear.

"Repeated drone and missile attacks are being attempted in the immediate vicinity of the vessel. The crew is living under constant fear of a direct hit at any moment," it said.

The FSUI urged the shipowners, the vessel's flag state, the relevant authorities and the government to intervene immediately to ensure the crew's safety and facilitate their evacuation.

"We urgently appeal to all concerned authorities, shipowners, flag state, and the Government of India to immediately secure their safety and arrange prompt repatriation," the union said.





Calling for urgent action, it added, "Indian seafarers must not be left as sitting targets in conflict zones. Act now."

This comes a day after MEA raised concerns with Ukraine over the safety of Indian seafarers in the Black Sea. On Monday, the MEA summoned Ukraine's ambassador to India, Dr Oleksandr Polishchuk, following an attack on the merchant vessel MV OMORFI near the Ukrainian port of Odesa that had four Indian crew members on board.

The MEA said the strike resulted in the death of an Indian national and condemned attacks on commercial shipping in the "strongest terms", calling them a threat to maritime safety, freedom of navigation and international commerce. It also urged Kyiv to ensure that commercial vessels carrying civilian seafarers are not targeted.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami distributes subsidies to boost clean mobility; flags off 11 clean fuel vehicles
World.content:
Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday distributed capital grant and incentive subsidy cheques to six primary beneficiary vehicle owners under the Uttarakhand Clean Mobility Transition Policy-2024 at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan, Chief Minister's Camp Office.

The transport department has also completed the subsidy approval process for five additional beneficiaries.

On the occasion, the CM flagged off 11 clean fuel-based vehicles. Addressing the programme, he said that the assistance was not merely financial support but a symbol of the state government's commitment to building a clean, modern, and environmentally sustainable transport system in Uttarakhand. He said the initiative would promote clean fuel-based public transport in urban areas, reduce pollution caused by diesel-powered vehicles, and strengthen environmental conservation efforts.

Dhami said the world is facing the serious challenge of climate change, making it essential to strike a balance between development and environmental protection. He emphasised that development is meaningful only when it remains in harmony with nature and ensures a safe and clean future for coming generations. The CM said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is emerging as a global leader in green energy and sustainable development.





He highlighted initiatives such as the country's target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, the Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) campaign, the PM e-Bus Sewa scheme, and the expansion of solar and other renewable energy sources as evidence of India's commitment to environmental protection.

Dhami said Uttarakhand, nestled in the Himalayas and revered as Devbhoomi, is the origin of life-giving rivers such as the Ganga and Yamuna.

He noted that the state's rich biodiversity, forests, rivers, and mountain ecosystems are invaluable national assets. Protecting the environment and maintaining ecological balance, he said, is a shared responsibility, adding that the state government's vision is to ensure that development and environmental conservation go hand in hand.The chief minister said that with this vision, the government has implemented the Uttarakhand Clean Mobility Transition Policy-2024.

The policy aims to modernise public transport in urban areas, reduce pollution caused by ageing diesel vehicles, and encourage the adoption of CNG and other clean fuel-based transport systems. He expressed confidence that the policy would lay a strong foundation for a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable transport network across the state. Dhami further said that the state government is continuously expanding the operation of electric buses in Dehradun, Haridwar, and Haldwani.

EV charging stations are also being established across Uttarakhand to provide the necessary infrastructure for clean mobility. He added that work is progressing rapidly on ropeway projects and modern urban transport systems, which will improve traffic management, reduce congestion and pollution in hilly regions, and make transportation safer and more environmentally friendly.

World.title: Delhi Police officer denies authorising alleged RAF pellet gun firing during CJP march: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A senior

officer has denied being present at the spot when a Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel allegedly fired from a pellet gun at protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) Parliament march on July 20, officials said on Tuesday.

A General Diary (GD) entry recorded by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) at Parliament Street police station mentions that the officer was present in Zone-1 near Jantar Mantar when the alleged incident took place, PTI reported.

The officer, however, claimed that he was nearly half a kilometre away from the spot when the pellet rounds were reportedly fired.

Meanwhile, a high-level meeting was held at the Delhi Police headquarters on Tuesday to discuss the GD entry related to the alleged use of non-lethal munitions, including plastic pellets, by the RAF, the specialised riot-control wing of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).

Attended by senior Delhi Police officers, the meeting focused on the circumstances surrounding the GD entry recorded on July 22 at 1:24 pm.

According to official police records, the GD entry was made ased on information provided by a Deputy Commandant-rank RAF officer. It states that RAF personnel deployed in Zone-1 alongside a Deputy Commissioner of Police-rank Delhi Police officer fired multiple non-lethal munitions after received rmission from the senior police officer.





According to the entry, the RAF fired 55 non-electrical shells, 15 electrical shells, five tear smoke grenades, two rounds from anti-riot guns and two rounds of plastic pellets while controlling the crowd.

Officials said one round of plastic pellets contains four plastic projectiles, which differ from metal pellets and are designed to cause less serious injuries.

The alleged use of plastic pellets has become a major political flashpoint after reports that some protesters sustained grievous pellet injuries during the violence.

Multiple Delhi Police, RAF and CRPF personnel were also injured in the clashes.

Delhi Police has maintained that allegations of the force using pellet guns against protesters are "false and misleading", reiterating its position in a statement on its official X handle. According to the police, more than 65 protesters and over 200 police personnel were injured during the clashes.

World.title: Artistes oppose bid to privatise Kolhapur’s Palace Theatre
World.content:
Artistes associated with the Sangeetsurya Keshavrao Bhosale Natyagruha, popularly known as the Palace Theatre, staged a protest on Tuesday to oppose the proposal to privatise the historic building in Maharashtra’s Kolhapur district.

The artistes demanded that the theatre remain under the control of the Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC). The civic body had passed a resolution on July 20 to hand over the building’s management to a private company.

“I have grown watching plays here. Many artistes started their career here as this place gave space for experimental theatre. With privatisation, it will all be gone. People doing experimental theatre will not get slots as the new manager will look to make profits,” said Prasad Jamdagni, an actor and organiser of musical shows.

The theatre, considered a centre of art and cultural heritage, was built in 1915 under the initiative of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, who ruled the princely state of Kolhapur between 1884 and 1922. It was then named after late singer-actor Keshavrao Bhosale.

₹35-crore renovation

The theatre is slated to be inaugurated on August 9 this year after it was gutted in a fire on August 8, 2024. According to the KMC, the State government had spent ₹35 crore to renovate the historic building.

Artistes also questioned the need for privatising the theatre at a time when it is well-equipped and set for inauguration.

Anand Kale, television and film actor, said, “The rangakarmis (artistes) have worked with the Kolhapur administration to renovate the Palace Theatre. Now that it is well-equipped, suddenly, why do they want to privatise it? Why not run it themselves and make it profitable? We are even willing to pay increased rent per show at the theatre.”

The artistes also highlighted that the theatre is located near the 25,000-seating capacity Khasbag Khusti Maidan, said to be India’s biggest wrestling stadium, where several theatre performances are also staged. They pointed out that a plan to build an exhibition hall on a plot adjacent to the theatre has also been sanctioned.

Before the fire incident, the rent for each show at the auditorium was ₹12,500. The artistes have expressed willingness to pay increased rent but want the theatre to be controlled by the KMC.

“If we do the math, with the renovated auditorium in place, the KMC can easily earn 1.20 crore per annum,” Mr. Kale said.

He based his calculation on the 450 slots that were booked the year before the fire took place and increased rent between ₹25,000 and ₹35,000.

‘Outsource services’

The artistes appealed to the KMC to outsource services, including security, cleaning, repairs and maintenance, and not hand over the theatre’s entire management to a private company. “If they [KMC officials] are so confident that the private firm can make profits, then why not form a team that can make profits for the KMC,” Mr. Jamdagni said.

Meanwhile, defending the move, KMC Commissioner Dr. Rajendra Bharud said privatisation will help the theatre sustain itself financially. “The decision was taken by the general body. The services are being privatised. KMC will still be jointly operating the theatre with the private player. It is my responsibility that transparency is maintained,” he said.

World.title: BJP bids to stave off JSP, RJD challenge as campaigning ends for Bankipur byelection
World.content:
Campaigning for the July 30 Bankipur Assembly byelection in Bihar came to a close on Tuesday, with candidates making a final push to secure the seat vacated by BJP national president Nitin Nabin following his election to the Rajya Sabha in April.

The BJP is making an all-out effort to retain the seat and has fielded 32-year-old youth wing leader Neeraj Kumar Sinha as its candidate. The bypoll will mark the electoral debut of Prashant Kishor, the 49-year-old founder of the Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), which failed to win any seat in the Assembly poll last year.

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has nominated Rekha Kumari, who was the runner-up from the seat in the Assembly poll that was won by Mr. Nabin by a margin of over 50,000 votes. RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav joined the party’s campaign only on Monday.

Although 25 candidates are in the fray, the contest appears to be primarily between the BJP and the JSP. The Bankipur constituency has nearly four lakh voters. The Kayasth and Yadav communities together account for about 25% of the electorate. Muslims and Chandravanshis also have sizeable numbers, with both communities constituting nearly 20% of the voters. The Vaishya, Dalit, Bhumihar, Rajput, Brahmin, Kurmi, and Kushwaha communities each make up between 3% and 8% of the electorate.

Key concerns

On the BJP candidate’s roadshow, Sanjay Gupta, a trader from Meethapur, said, “We are not looking at caste; for us, the candidate is more important.”

Voters also expressed concern over issues such as the NEET paper leak row and alleged theft of donations at Ram Temple.

Mr. Kishor addressed public meetings in Peermuhani, Sabzibagh, and Jai Prakash Nagar. Speaking to the gathering at Peermuhani, the JSP leader said, “When you go to cast the vote, think about the future of your children.”

Mr. Nabin will be present in Patna on the day of voting, though he is not a voter of Bankipur. He is a voter of the Digha Assembly constituency. The results will be declared on August 3.

World.title: Assam floods: Death toll reaches 75, MLAs to donate a month’s salary for flood relief
World.content:
A day after inviting criticism for his “insensitive” social media post enjoying a meal with some MLAs at the Assam Assembly canteen, Speaker Ranjeet Kumar Dass on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) announced that he and Deputy Speaker Habbey Teron would donate a month’s salary toward relief and rehabilitation of the flood-affected people in the State.

The Speaker also announced that all the staff of the Assam Legislative Assembly Secretariat would donate a day’s salary for the victims of the floods that have claimed 75 lives so far, displaced more than 7.5 lakh people, and washed away thousands of livestock.

Barring two of Raijor Dal, all MLAs from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its regional allies Asom Gana Parishad and Bodoland People’s Front, and the opposition Congress, All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF), and Trinamool Congress pledged a month’s salary for flood relief.

While Raijor Dal MLAs Akhil Gogoi and Mehboob Mukhtar have been on the ground, providing relief materials to the flood-hit, AIUDF legislator Mazibur Rahman said the two party MLAs would contribute a month’s salary for the “noble cause” despite party president Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal having committed ₹2 crore for the flood victims.

On July 26, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma appealed to all BJP workers to donate generously for the flood victims. He advised party workers to hand over donations of up to ₹2,000 to the local MLA and deposit amounts exceeding ₹2,000 in the BJP Assam’s bank account.

In eastern Assam’s Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat, the three worst-affected districts, people began returning home to assess the damage and salvage what was left. Amid the despair, stench of rotting animal carcasses, soggy conditions, and the possibility of diseases, many victims vented their anger on the government and rescue agencies for not reacting promptly enough.

Earlier, the Chief Minister said that the people and the district authorities in the three districts, not used to floods, were least prepared for the unprecedented deluge almost overnight due to extremely heavy rainfall in adjoining areas of Assam and Nagaland.

Some used sarcasm to underscore the anger. “Thank you, government of India, government of Assam, Indian armed forces, paramilitary forces, NDRF, SDRF and all government agencies for acting so fast in rescue operations during flood in Assam,” a Sivasagar town resident, the first floor of whose house was submerged, wrote on his social media handle.

National problem tag sought

In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), the All Assam Students’ Union (AASU) demanded that Assam’s flood-and-erosion issue be declared a national problem, warranting sustained national commitment and intervention for a permanent solution.

Requesting the Prime Minister to visit the flood-affected areas of the severely affected districts of Sivasagar, Charaideo and Jorhat at the earliest, the AASU reminded him of his frequent visits to the State for election campaigns.

“At this hour of unprecedented suffering, they [affected people] equally deserve your presence, solidarity, and assurance,” the letter signed by AASU president Utpal Sarma and general secretary Samiran Phukan read.

The AASU also urged the Prime Minister to announce a special economic package for the three hardest-hit districts to ensure comprehensive relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction, and constitute a high-level fact-finding committee comprising independent experts to ascertain the causes of this catastrophe and prepare a time-bound roadmap for a permanent and scientific solution.

Another youth body, the Asom Jatiyatabadi Yuba Chatra Parishad, urged the Assam government to significantly enhance relief and rehabilitation measures for flood-affected people, including increasing the one-time ex gratia for families of those killed in the floods to ₹20 lakh.

World.title: Stop ‘witch-hunt of students’ or brace for new stir: CJP to govt.
World.content:
A day after warning of fresh protests over the Centre’s alleged violation of the assurance that no punitive action would be taken against protesters, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday called on the government to stop “targeting and witch-hunting” students.

“If the harassment of students at the hands of the police continues, the Cockroach Janta Party will respond with a massive peaceful protest soon,” he posted on X.

The Bihar government said it had withdrawn FIRs against protesters registered before 6 p.m. on July 26, and the governments of Assam and West Bengal have followed suit. However, there has been no word from Delhi Police on the issue so far.

When reached for comment, Delhi Police PRO declined to comment. Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said, “We have not received any orders or official communication to withdraw the FIRs yet.”

The police have not made any arrests in the case so far. A total of 14 FIRs were registered and 600 people were detained and subsequently released in the South East district where the prohibitory orders were imposed.

On July 25, the 36th day of the protest, the CJP called off its stir after the Centre agreed to its three main demands — ouster of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union Education Minister, compensation for the families of those who ended their lives after the cancellation of NEET on May 3, and withdrawal of FIRs against the protesters and an assurance that no future action would be taken against them.

‘Credible apprehension’
